definition_zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；（统计）总体
definition_en: the people living in a place, or any group of individuals counted together, including a breeding group of animals or a complete set of data
core_image: 一张城市鸟瞰图，屋顶密密麻麻，每个小点代表一个人，远处还有一片标着虫鸟的林子
scene: The city's population doubled in twenty years, and the water supply never caught up.
sceneCN: 这里 population 是「人口、居民总数」（第 1 个义项：某地居民的整体数量）；句意：这座城市的人口在二十年间翻了一番，供水却始终没跟上。图中可辨识物件：密集屋顶、代表居民的小点、远处的林地与鸟群。

pos.zh: 人口；全体居民；种群；总体

senses.title: People counted together
senses.titleCN: 人口：一地居民的总数
senses.definition: the total number of people who live in a particular area, town or country
senses.definitionCN: 居住在某一地区、城镇或国家的总人数
senses.example: The population of the region passed five million last year.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区的人口去年突破五百万。
senses.why: populus in Latin meant 'the people'. The suffix -ation turns the body of people into a countable quantity, so the word names people as a number.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 populus 意为“人民”。后缀 -ation 把一群人变成可计数的量，因此这个词把“人”命名为一个数字。

senses.title: The people themselves
senses.titleCN: 全体居民：住在那里的人
senses.definition: all the inhabitants of a place, thought of as a social body rather than as a statistic
senses.definitionCN: 某地的全部居民，被视为一个社会群体而非一个统计数字
senses.example: The new bus route mainly serves the rural population.
senses.exampleCN: 这条新公交线路主要服务农村居民。
senses.why: English often uses population for the living community, not merely its size. The same word shifts from number to people by context alone.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用 population 指活生生的社区，而不只是它的规模。同一个词凭语境从“数字”滑向“人群”。

senses.title: A named subgroup
senses.titleCN: 特定人群：某类人构成的那一群
senses.definition: a particular group within a larger community, such as students, patients or workers
senses.definitionCN: 较大社区中的某一特定群体，如学生、病人或劳动者
senses.example: The clinic serves a mainly elderly population.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所主要服务老年人群。
senses.why: Any bounded group can be called a population because the word only requires a set of individuals and a shared boundary.
senses.whyCN: 任何有边界的群体都可称作 population，因为这个词只要求“一群个体”加“一条共同边界”。

senses.title: Biology: one breeding group
senses.titleCN: 生物学：一个繁殖种群
senses.definition: in biology, a group of organisms of the same species living in one area and able to interbreed
senses.definitionCN: 生物学上指同一物种、生活在同一区域且能相互交配繁殖的一群生物
senses.example: The island population of finches has been isolated for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的雀鸟种群已隔离了几个世纪。
senses.why: Biologists borrowed the demographic word and replaced 'citizens' with 'individuals of one species'. The boundary, not the species, defines the group.
senses.whyCN: 生物学家借用了人口学的词，把“公民”换成“同一物种的个体”。界定群体的是边界，而不是物种。

senses.title: Statistics: the whole set
senses.titleCN: 统计学：总体（与样本相对）
senses.definition: in statistics, the complete set of items from which a sample is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 统计学上指被抽样的完整集合，与“样本”相对
senses.example: The sample was chosen randomly from a population of ten thousand firms.
senses.exampleCN: 样本是从一万家企业的总体中随机抽出的。
senses.why: Statistics keeps the demographic sense of 'everyone', then applies it to any complete set: once you can count a group, the group is a population.
senses.whyCN: 统计学保留“全部人”的人口学含义，再套到任何完整集合上：只要能计数一群，这群就是总体。

senses.title: Animal or plant numbers
senses.titleCN: 动植物数量：一个地区的个体量
senses.definition: the number of animals or plants of a kind in a given area, often studied as density or trend
senses.definitionCN: 某一地区某类动植物的个体数量，常以密度或变化趋势来研究
senses.example: The wolf population fell sharply after the hard winter.
senses.exampleCN: 严冬之后狼的数量大幅下降。
senses.why: The counting frame is the key: pick a place and a kind, and the word reports how many are inside it.
senses.whyCN: 关键在于计数框：选定一个地方和一个种类，这个词就报告框里有多少个。

senses.title: The act of settling
senses.titleCN: 迁入定居：使地方有人住（旧义）
senses.definition: the act of filling an area with inhabitants, now mostly expressed by the related verb
senses.definitionCN: 使某地住满居民的行为，现多由相关动词表达
senses.example: The population of the frontier took three generations.
senses.exampleCN: 边疆的移民定居用了三代人的时间。
senses.why: The suffix -ation can name an action as well as a result. This older sense survives in the verb populate and in historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ation 既能命名结果，也能命名动作。这个较旧的义项保留在动词 populate 与历史写作中。

senses.title: A demographic problem
senses.titleCN: 人口结构：政策讨论里的对象
senses.definition: the size and age structure of a society considered as an economic or political issue
senses.definitionCN: 把社会的规模与年龄结构当作经济或政治问题来看待
senses.example: An ageing population puts pressure on pensions and hospitals.
senses.exampleCN: 人口老龄化给养老金和医院带来压力。
senses.why: Once governments began counting citizens for policy, population became a problem to be managed, not just a fact to be reported.
senses.whyCN: 当政府开始为政策清点公民，population 就从“被报告的事实”变成“待管理的问题”。

intro.en: Population comes from Latin populus 'the people' through populatio 'a peopling, a laying waste'. The word entered English in the 16th century on the Latin stem populatio(n-).
intro.cn: population 经由拉丁语 populatio“使人居住；蹂躏”上溯到 populus“人民”。16 世纪以拉丁词干 populatio(n-) 进入英语。

items.en: populus meant 'the people' as a body. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it may come from Etruscan, and no reliable Latin root can be given, so the deeper layer should be marked as uncertain in origin.
items.cn: populus 指作为整体的“人民”。其更深来源不确定，可能来自伊特鲁里亚语，无法给出可靠的拉丁词根，因此更深一层应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: populatio in classical Latin could mean both 'a peopling, settlement' and 'a devastating, laying waste'. The two senses seem to come from two verbs that looked alike.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语中 populatio 既可指“使人定居”，也可指“蹂躏、毁坏”。两个义项似乎来自两个外形相近的动词。

items.en: English takes the word in the 1500s first as 'the peopling of a place', then quickly as 'the number of inhabitants'.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪先取“使地方有人居住”之义，随后很快转为“居民数量”。

items.en: With the growth of censuses in the 18th and 19th centuries, population becomes the standard word for an official count of residents.
items.cn: 18 至 19 世纪人口普查兴起，population 成为官方居民统计的标准用词。

items.en: In the 20th century biology adopts the word for any interbreeding group, transferring the census idea from citizens to individuals of one species.
items.cn: 20 世纪生物学借用该词指任何能相互繁殖的群体，把人口普查的思路从公民转到同一物种的个体。

items.en: Statistics completes the abstraction: the population is now any complete set from which a sample is drawn.
items.cn: 统计学完成了抽象化：population 现在指任何被抽样的完整集合。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the popul- shape and the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group shares the idea of people or counted individuals but differs in what is being counted.
note.cn: 形近组共享 popul- 外形与同一拉丁词干；近义组都涉及“人”或“被计数的个体”，差别在计数对象。

entries.definition: full of people, densely inhabited. It describes a place, while population names the people or their number.
entries.definitionCN: 人口稠密的；住满人的。它描述地方，而 population 命名人或其数量。

entries.definition: to fill an area with people or animals. It names the act that produces a population.
entries.definitionCN: 居住于；使有人居住。它命名产生 population 的那个动作。

entries.definition: liked by many people. It goes back to populus too, but through the sense 'of the people', not through counting them.
entries.definitionCN: 受欢迎的。它同样上溯到 populus，但走的是“属于人民的”这条义线，而不是计数。

entries.definition: the people who live in a place. It names them directly, while population can mean either the people or their count.
entries.definitionCN: 居民。它直接命名人，而 population 既可指人也可指数量。

entries.definition: people with legal membership in a state. It is a legal category, while population is a demographic count that includes non-citizens.
entries.definitionCN: 公民。它是法律范畴，而 population 是包含非公民的人口统计。

entries.definition: a group linked by shared place or interests. It stresses relationships, while population stresses mere co-presence and number.
entries.definitionCN: 社区；群体。它强调关系，而 population 强调共同在场与数量。

entries.definition: the statistical structure of a population, such as age and income. It analyses a population rather than naming it.
entries.definitionCN: 人口结构。指年龄、收入等统计构成，是对 population 的分析而非命名。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: popul- is the stem of Latin populus 'people', so population and popular sit in the same family.
normal.cn: popul- 是拉丁 populus“人民”的词干，所以 population 与 popular 同属一族。

normal.en: The -ation suffix turns people into a countable quantity, which is why the word collocates with growth, density and decline.
normal.cn: -ation 后缀把“人”变成可计量的量，所以这个词常与增长、密度、下降搭配。

normal.en: population density is arithmetic made visible: people divided by area.
normal.cn: 人口密度就是可视化的算术：人数除以面积。

normal.en: In biology the census frame is kept but the citizens become finches, wolves or trees.
normal.cn: 生物学保留了普查的计数框，只把公民换成了雀鸟、狼或树木。

normal.en: In statistics population is the whole set, and sample is the part taken from it.
normal.cn: 统计学里总体是全集，样本是从中取出的部分。

abstract.en: Picture a map covered with dots, then zoom in until each dot becomes a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张布满小点的地图，再放大到每个点变成一张脸。

abstract.en: Picture a census form that asks one question only: how many of you are there?
abstract.cn: 想象一张只问一个问题的普查表：你们有多少人？

abstract.en: Picture a jar of seeds: the jar is the statistical population, the handful you test is the sample.
abstract.cn: 想象一罐种子：罐子是统计总体，抓出来试的一把是样本。

examples.en: Population growth slowed once the factories closed.
examples.cn: 工厂关闭后，人口增长放缓了。

examples.en: The study tracked a population of six hundred patients over five years.
examples.cn: 该研究在五年间追踪了六百名患者组成的人群。

examples.en: Statisticians distinguish the population from the sample drawn out of it.
examples.cn: 统计学家把总体与从中抽取的样本区别开来。

dict_mnemonic.text: “泡皮溜”音近 population：一群人泡在水里、皮都溜滑——人多得像下饺子 → population 人口

root: 拉丁 populus“人民”（更深来源不确定，可能出自伊特鲁里亚语）；populatio(n-) 词干 + -ation 名词后缀。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all answer one question with different boundaries: how many are inside this frame?
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在回答同一个问题，只是换边界：这个框里有多少？

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map of dots, each dot a person.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张由小点构成的地图，每个点是一个人。

branches.en: COUNT AND BODY: the number and the living community are one word seen twice, once as arithmetic and once as society.
branches.cn: 数字与群体：数量与活生生的社区是同一个词的两种看法，一是算术，一是社会。

branches.en: NAMED SUBGROUP: students, patients and workers each get their own population once a boundary is drawn.
branches.cn: 特定人群：一旦画出边界，学生、病人、劳动者各自成一个人群。

branches.en: NON-HUMAN COUNT: breeding groups and wildlife numbers apply the census frame to other species.
branches.cn: 非人类计数：繁殖群体与野生动物数量把普查的框套到其他物种上。

branches.en: STATISTICAL WHOLE: the population is whatever complete set a sample is taken from.
branches.cn: 统计总体：population 就是任何被抽样的完整集合。

branches.en: PROCESS AND POLICY: settling an area and managing an ageing society are the verb side and the political side of the same noun.
branches.cn: 过程与政策：让人定居与管理老龄化社会，是同一名词的动词面与政治面。

intro.en: Population is the Latin stem popul- plus -ation. The suffix marks a result or an action, and the same stem yields the adjective populous and the verb populate.
intro.cn: population 是拉丁词干 popul- 加 -ation。后缀标记结果或动作，同一词干还产出形容词 populous 与动词 populate。

latinIntro.en: The Latin family runs from populus 'people' to populatio 'settlement, devastation' and populosus 'full of people'. English keeps popul- throughout.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词族从 populus“人民”延伸到 populatio“定居、毁坏”与 populosus“人多的”。英语始终保留 popul-。

items.meaning: to fill a place with inhabitants
items.meaningCN: 居住于；使有人居住（popul-“人民”+ -ate 动词后缀）
items.example: Settlers populated the valley within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 定居者十年内就住满了这个山谷。

items.meaning: the people of an area or a counted group
items.meaningCN: 人口；种群（-ion 构成结果名词）
items.example: The population is estimated at two million.
It is the most populous province in the country.
items.exampleCN: 它是全国人口最多的省份。

items.meaning: the loss of inhabitants from an area
items.example: Rural depopulation has closed many schools.
items.exampleCN: 农村人口流失使许多学校关闭。

items.meaning: too many people for the resources available
items.exampleCN: 人口过剩使供水系统吃紧。

items.meaning: liked or accepted by many people
items.meaningCN: 受欢迎的；大众的（-ar“属于……的”）
items.example: The measure is popular with younger voters.
items.exampleCN: 该措施受年轻选民欢迎。

items.meaning: a politician who appeals to ordinary people
items.meaningCN: 民粹主义者（-ist 指“以人民名义行事者”）
items.example: The populist won by attacking experts.
items.exampleCN: 这位民粹主义者靠攻击专家赢得选举。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 人民；国民（更深来源不确定）

latinEntries.meaning: a peopling, settlement; also a laying waste
the popular party in Roman politics
latinEntries.meaningCN: 平民派（罗马政治中的“人民派”）

definition_zh: 潜在地；有可能地；从潜力上看
definition_en: in a way that is possible but not yet actual, describing what could happen or what a thing could become
core_image: 一颗包在种皮里的种子，旁边虚线的树影已经画好，但树还没长出来
scene: The new strain is potentially resistant to every drug we have.
sceneCN: 这里 potentially 是「有可能地、潜在地」（第 1 个义项：可能出现但尚未发生）；句意：这种新菌株有可能对我们现有的所有药物都耐药。图中可辨识物件：包着种皮的种子、虚线勾勒的树影、尚未长出的枝条。

pos.zh: 潜在地；有可能地；从潜力上看

senses.title: Possible but not actual
senses.titleCN: 潜在地：可能但还没发生
senses.definition: used to say that something may happen or may be true, without asserting that it does
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明某事可能发生或可能成立，但不肯定它已经发生或成立
senses.example: The drug is potentially effective, but no trial has been completed.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药可能有疗效，但还没有完成试验。
senses.why: potentia in Latin is 'power, capacity'. The adverb marks a capacity that exists before any result, so the statement stays open.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 potentia 是“力量、能力”。这个副词标记先于结果存在的能力，所以陈述保持开放。

senses.title: A latent power
senses.titleCN: 从潜力上看：能力还没释放
senses.definition: with respect to the capacity a person or thing still holds inside and has not yet used
senses.definitionCN: 从人或事物内部尚未释放的能力来看
senses.example: The team is potentially the strongest in the league.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在潜力上是联赛最强的。
senses.why: Here the word measures stored capacity rather than probability. The ranking is about what could be released, not about odds.
senses.whyCN: 这里它衡量的是储存的能力，而非概率。排名评的是可能释放的力量，不是赔率。

senses.title: Risk warning
senses.titleCN: 可能有危害：先提醒再说
senses.definition: used to flag a possible danger while leaving the certainty of that danger unstated
senses.definitionCN: 用于提示可能存在的危险，同时不说明危险的确定程度
senses.example: The chemical is potentially harmful to children.
senses.exampleCN: 这种化学物质可能对儿童有害。
senses.why: Risk language needs a word that names danger without proving it. The adverb lets a warning be urgent and still cautious.
senses.whyCN: 风险语言需要一个既指出危险又不证明危险的词。这个副词让警告既有紧迫感又保持谨慎。

senses.title: Tentative scientific claim
senses.titleCN: 在科研表述里留余地
senses.definition: in scientific writing, used to report an inference whose evidence is indirect
senses.definitionCN: 在科学写作中，用于报告证据为间接的推论
senses.example: The pattern is potentially caused by a shift in ocean currents.
senses.exampleCN: 这一模式可能是由洋流变化造成的。
senses.why: Science separates observation from explanation. The adverb marks the step from data to a proposed cause, which is exactly where certainty drops.
senses.whyCN: 科学要把观察与解释分开。这个副词标记从数据迈到所提原因的那一步，而确定性正在这一步下降。

senses.title: Untapped resource
senses.titleCN: 可争取的资源：还没用上
senses.definition: describing a resource, market or worker whose value is available if it is used
senses.definitionCN: 描述资源、市场或劳动者只要被使用就有价值
senses.example: The region is potentially a major market for electric cars.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区可能成为电动汽车的重要市场。
senses.why: Economics uses the word for value that exists in possibility. The resource is real; only its use is missing.
senses.whyCN: 经济学用它指存在于可能性中的价值。资源是真实的，缺的只是使用。

senses.title: Mathematics and physics
senses.titleCN: 数学物理：潜在的量
senses.definition: in physics, describing a quantity defined at a point and realized only when something moves or changes
senses.definitionCN: 在物理学中描述某点上的量，只有发生移动或变化时才实现
senses.example: Energy is stored in the field as a potential difference.
senses.exampleCN: 能量以电势差的形式储存在场中。
senses.why: Physics gives the word its most literal sense: potential energy is energy by position, waiting for a release.
senses.whyCN: 物理学给了这个词最字面的义项：势能是按位置拥有的能量，等着被释放。

senses.title: Hedging in argument
senses.titleCN: 论证中留退路
senses.definition: used in debate to weaken a claim so that it cannot be refuted too easily
senses.definitionCN: 在辩论中用来弱化主张，使其不易被轻易驳倒
senses.example: This approach is potentially more fair, though the data are thin.
senses.exampleCN: 这一做法可能更公平，尽管数据很少。
senses.why: The adverb is a hedge: it transfers the burden of proof from the speaker to future evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词是一种模糊限制：把举证责任从说话人转给未来的证据。

senses.title: Possibility in grammar
senses.titleCN: 语法上的可能语气
senses.definition: in grammar teaching, labelling an adverb that expresses possibility rather than certainty
senses.definitionCN: 在语法教学中标记表达可能性而非确定性的副词
senses.example: Potentially is a possibility adverb, like perhaps and conceivably.
senses.exampleCN: potentially 是可能性副词，与“也许”“可以想象地”等词同类。
senses.why: Grammar groups words by what they do to a sentence's certainty. This adverb lowers certainty without cancelling the statement.
senses.whyCN: 语法按“对句子确定性的作用”给词分组。这个副词降低确定性，但不取消陈述。

intro.en: Potentially is potential plus -ly. Potential comes from Latin potentia 'power, ability', from potens 'able, powerful', itself the present participle of posse 'to be able'.
intro.cn: potentially 是 potential 加 -ly。potential 来自拉丁语 potentia“力量、能力”，源于 potens“有能力的”，而 potens 是 posse“能够”的现在分词。

items.en: posse 'to be able' is a contraction of potis esse 'to be able'. potis is an old adjective meaning 'able, capable'.
items.cn: posse“能够”是 potis esse“有能力存在”的缩合。potis 是古形容词，意为“有能力的”。

items.en: The present participle potens 'being able' produced the adjective 'powerful'. From it English takes potent and potency.
items.cn: 现在分词 potens“有能力的”产生形容词“强有力的”。英语由此取得 potent 与 potency。

items.en: potentia abstracted the adjective into a noun: 'power, capacity, force'. The noun could mean capacity in the sense of what a thing can become.
items.cn: potentia 把形容词抽象为名词：力量、能力、势力。该名词也可指事物可能成为的那种“能力”。

items.en: English forms potential in the 14th century as an adjective from the Latin stem. The noun use 'capacity for future success' appears later.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪以拉丁词干构成形容词 potential。指“未来成功的潜力”的名词用法出现较晚。

items.en: The -ly adverb is formed on the adjective and spreads in scientific and journalistic prose, where claims need hedging.
items.cn: -ly 副词由该形容词构成，在科学与新闻写作中扩散，因为这些文体需要为论断留余地。

items.en: Physics fixes the meaning in potential energy and potential difference, where the quantity is real but unrealized.
items.cn: 物理学在势能与电势差中固定了词义：该量真实存在但尚未实现。

note.en: The look-alike group all contains pot- from potis or from a different root; the near-meaning group shares the idea of possibility but differs in strength.
note.cn: 形近组都含 pot-，或同出 potis，或另有来源；近义组都表“可能”，差别在可能性强度。

entries.definition: existing as a capacity rather than as an act. The adjective modifies a noun; the adverb modifies a whole claim.
entries.definitionCN: 潜在的；潜力。形容词修饰名词，副词修饰整个论断。

entries.definition: strong in effect, especially of a drug or argument. It states present power, not future possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 强效的；有力的。它陈述当下的力量，不是未来的可能。

entries.definition: safe to drink. It looks close but comes from Latin potare 'to drink', not from posse.
entries.definitionCN: 可饮用的。它外形接近，但来自拉丁 potare“喝”，并非 posse。

entries.definition: perhaps; used for plain uncertainty. It is more neutral and less technical than potentially.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；可能。用于一般的不确定，比 potentially 更中性、更少术语色彩。

entries.definition: in a way that can be imagined even if unlikely. It often signals a distant possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 可以想象地。即使不太可能也能想到，常暗示较远的可能性。

entries.definition: as may reasonably be supposed. It reports an inference from evidence, not a bare possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 大概；据推测。它报告基于证据的推断，不是单纯的可能。

entries.definition: as can be supported by argument. It hedges a judgment, while potentially hedges a prediction.
entries.definitionCN: 可以说是。它为判断留余地，而 potentially 为预测留余地。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: potent- is the stem of 'having power', so potentially means 'with power still held in reserve'.
normal.cn: potent- 是“有力量”的词干，所以 potentially 意为“力量还握在手里未用”。

normal.en: Potential energy in physics is the cleanest model: the energy is there, the movement has not started.
normal.cn: 物理学的势能是最清楚的模型：能量在那里，运动还没开始。

normal.en: In warnings, potentially harmful and potentially fatal pair with the same hedging job.
normal.cn: 在警示语中，可能有危害与可能致命承担同样的留余地功能。

normal.en: Potential plus -ly keeps the adjective visible, so the adverb never claims more than the adjective does.
normal.cn: potential 加 -ly 仍看得见形容词，所以副词声称的绝不超过形容词。

normal.en: The paired noun is potential: a player with potential is one whose value is not yet shown.
normal.cn: 对应名词是 potential：有潜力的选手就是价值尚未展现的人。

abstract.en: Picture a seed in a drawer: the tree is fully possible and completely absent at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象抽屉里的一颗种子：那棵树既完全可能，又完全不在。

abstract.en: Picture a door that is unlocked but has never been opened.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没锁、却从未被推开的门。

abstract.en: Picture a battery on a shelf: voltage is present, current is not flowing.
abstract.cn: 想象架子上的一节电池：电压在，电流没走。

examples.en: The virus is potentially more contagious than earlier variants.
examples.cn: 这种病毒可能比早期变种更具传染性。

examples.en: She is potentially the best candidate, but she has not applied.
examples.cn: 她可能是最佳人选，但她还没申请。

examples.en: Potentially, the new method could cut costs by a third.
examples.cn: 从可能性上说，新方法能把成本削减三分之一。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破摊子里”音近 potentially：破摊子里也许藏着好东西——只是“有可能” → potentially 潜在地

root: 拉丁 posse“能够”（potis esse 的缩合）→ potens“有能力的”→ potentia“力量、能力”；potential + -ly 构成副词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower the certainty of a statement while keeping the thing described fully real.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在降低陈述的确定性，同时让所描述之物保持真实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seed holding a tree that has not grown.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗种子，里面装着还没长出的树。

branches.en: HEDGING: the everyday possibility claim and the debater's hedge both keep the statement open to revision.
branches.cn: 留余地：日常的可能性陈述与辩论中的模糊限制，都让论断保留修改空间。

branches.en: CAPACITY HELD: a strong team and an unused market are both value that exists before it is spent.
branches.cn: 握有的能力：强队与未开发市场都是尚未花掉就已存在的价值。

branches.en: WARNING: risk language names a danger without having to prove it.
branches.cn: 警示：风险语言指出危险，而不必先证明危险。

branches.en: GRAMMATICAL STANCE: scientific inference and grammar teaching both treat the word as a marker of lowered certainty.
branches.cn: 语法立场：科学推论与语法教学都把这个词当作降低确定性的标记。

branches.en: PHYSICS: potential energy and potential difference give the metaphor a measurable form.
branches.cn: 物理学：势能与电势差给这个比喻一个可测量的形态。

intro.en: Potentially is built from the Latin stem potent- plus the English suffix -ly. The -ia and -ia/-cy nouns and the -ent adjective belong to the same family.
intro.cn: potentially 由拉丁词干 potent- 加英语后缀 -ly 构成。-ia 名词、-cy 名词与 -ent 形容词同属一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin connects potis 'able' to posse 'be able' and potens 'able', from which potentia and English potent derive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把 potis“有能力的”、posse“能够”、potens“有能力的”串起来，potentia 与英语 potent 由此而来。

items.meaningCN: 潜在的；潜力（-ial 构成形容词）
items.example: We have a potential buyer for the site.
items.exampleCN: 这块地有一位潜在买家。

items.meaningCN: 潜在地；有可能地（-ly 构成副词）
items.exampleCN: 这一变化可能意义重大。

items.meaningCN: 强效的；有力的（分词词干作形容词）

items.example: The potency of the drug declines with heat.

items.meaning: to increase the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 增强药效（-iate 动词后缀）
items.exampleCN: 该化合物增强了抗生素的效果。

items.example: The agency was impotent against the cartel.
items.exampleCN: 该机构对这个卡特尔无能为力。

items.example: The novel gives its ruler omnipotent powers.
items.exampleCN: 小说赋予统治者全能的力量。

items.meaning: dominant in inheritance, a genetics term
items.meaningCN: 遗传上优先显性的（pre-“在前”+ potent）
items.example: A prepotent gene masks the weaker one.
items.exampleCN: 优先显性的基因会掩盖较弱的那一个。

latinEntries.meaning: to be able, to have power

definition_en: a statement about what will happen in the future, especially one based on evidence, a model or reasoning
core_image: 一个人站在河边，手里拿着一张写着明天水位高度的纸条，纸条边缘还标着刻度
scene: The model's prediction was wrong by only two centimetres.
sceneCN: 这里 prediction 是「预测结果、预报」（第 1 个义项：关于未来的陈述）；句意：这个模型的预测只差了两厘米。图中可辨识物件：写有水位的纸条、刻度线、河岸与水位标尺。

senses.title: A statement about the future
senses.titleCN: 预测：对将发生之事的说法
senses.definition: a statement that something will happen, made before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 在某事发生之前说明它将会发生的陈述
senses.example: Her prediction that the bridge would fail proved right.
senses.exampleCN: 她关于这座桥会垮塌的预测被证明是对的。
senses.why: prae- means 'before' and dicere means 'say'. A prediction is literally something said before the event.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为“在前”，dicere 意为“说”。prediction 字面上就是在事件之前说出的东西。

senses.title: The act of foretelling
senses.titleCN: 预言的行为：说在前头
senses.definition: the act or practice of saying what will happen, rather than the content said
senses.definitionCN: 说明将会发生什么的行为或做法，而非说出的内容本身
senses.example: Prediction is easy; being right is hard.
senses.exampleCN: 预言很容易，说准却很难。
senses.why: The -ion suffix can name an action. English keeps both readings, the act and its product, in one noun.
senses.whyCN: -ion 后缀既可命名动作。英语把“行为”与“产物”两种读法都留在同一个名词里。

senses.title: Scientific forecast
senses.titleCN: 科学预报：可检验的说法
senses.definition: a precise statement derived from a theory or model that observation can confirm or refute
senses.definitionCN: 由理论或模型推出、可被观察证实或否证的精确陈述
senses.example: A good theory yields predictions that can be tested.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论会产生可被检验的预测。
senses.why: Science turns prophecy into a test: a prediction that cannot fail is not a scientific prediction.
senses.whyCN: 科学把预言变成检验：不可能失败的预测算不上科学预测。

senses.title: Model output
senses.titleCN: 模型输出：算出来的那个数
senses.definition: the value or outcome produced by a statistical or computational model for an unknown case
senses.definitionCN: 统计或计算模型对未知情形给出的数值或结果
senses.example: The prediction for next quarter is a small rise in demand.
senses.exampleCN: 对下季度的预测是需求小幅上升。
senses.why: Models produce numbers, and the industry borrowed the everyday word for them. The output inherits the word's forward-looking direction.
senses.whyCN: 模型产出数字，业界借用了日常词来称呼它。这个输出继承了该词“朝前看”的方向。

senses.title: Forecast of a trend
senses.titleCN: 趋势预报：把线往后画
senses.definition: an estimate of a future quantity based on extending a current pattern
senses.definitionCN: 通过延长当前模式而得到的未来数量估计
senses.example: Population predictions suggest the town will shrink after 2030.
senses.exampleCN: 人口预测显示该镇在 2030 年后会萎缩。
senses.why: Extending a line is the simplest picture of prediction, and it explains why forecasters speak of trends rather than events.
senses.whyCN: 把线延长是预测最简单的画面，也解释了为什么预报者谈趋势而不谈单个事件。

senses.title: Prophecy and omen
senses.titleCN: 古老意义上的预言
senses.definition: in older usage, a declaration of future events attributed to inspiration or divine knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 较旧用法中指被认为来自灵感或神启的未来事件宣告
senses.example: The prediction in the old chronicle was read as a warning.
senses.exampleCN: 旧编年史中的那则预言被解读为警告。
senses.why: Before statistics, prediction belonged to prophets. The word still carries a faint trace of that authority.
senses.whyCN: 在统计学之前，预测属于先知。这个词仍带着一点那种权威的痕迹。

senses.title: Prediction in betting
senses.titleCN: 下注前的判断
senses.definition: a guess about a result on which money or reputation may be staked
senses.definitionCN: 对某个结果作出的判断，可能据此押上金钱或名誉
senses.example: His prediction of the final score won him the office pool.
senses.exampleCN: 他对最终比分的预测让他赢下了办公室的赌局。
senses.why: A bet makes a prediction costly. The word gains weight when being wrong has a price.
senses.whyCN: 下注让预测有了代价。当猜错要付钱时，这个词就变得有分量。

senses.title: Prediction versus explanation
senses.titleCN: 与解释相对：说将来而非说为何
senses.definition: in philosophy of science, the forward-looking counterpart of an explanation of what has already happened
senses.definitionCN: 在科学哲学中，与对已发生之事的解释相对的那个朝前的部分
senses.example: The same law can serve as explanation and as prediction.
senses.exampleCN: 同一条定律既可作解释，也可作预测。
senses.why: Philosophers split the two directions of a theory: backward to causes, forward to predictions. One law, two uses.
senses.whyCN: 哲学家把理论的两个方向分开：向后找原因，向前作预测。同一条定律，两种用途。

intro.en: Prediction comes from Latin praedicere 'to say beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus dicere 'to say, tell'. The noun is praedictio.
intro.cn: prediction 来自拉丁语 praedicere“预先说出”，由 prae-“在前”加 dicere“说、告诉”构成，名词为 praedictio。

items.en: dicere meant 'to say, tell, declare'. It is the source of dictate, dictionary and verdict, and it is not the same root as dicare 'to dedicate'.
items.cn: dicere 意为“说、告诉、宣告”。它是 dictate、dictionary、verdict 的来源，与 dicare“奉献、宣布”并非同一词根。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus dicere produced praedicere, 'to say beforehand, foretell'. The prefix is temporal, not spatial.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 dicere 构成 praedicere“预先说出、预言”。这个前缀是时间性的，不是空间性的。

items.en: The action noun praedictio covered both 'a foretelling' and 'a proclamation'. Church Latin used it for prophetic declaration.
items.cn: 动作名词 praedictio 兼指“预言”与“宣告”。教会拉丁语用它指先知式的宣告。

items.en: English borrows prediction in the 1500s, first in religious and astrological writing about foretelling the future.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 prediction，最早见于关于预言的宗教与占星写作。

items.en: From the 17th century the word moves into natural philosophy, where a prediction must be testable against observation.
items.cn: 17 世纪起，这个词进入自然哲学，预测必须能被观察检验。

items.en: In the 20th century prediction becomes the standard term for a model's output, and machine learning makes it routine.
items.cn: 20 世纪，prediction 成为模型输出的标准说法，机器学习让它成为日常用语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -dict- stem or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group shares the forward look but differs in basis and certainty.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -dict- 词干或 pre- 前缀；近义组都朝前看，差别在依据与确定性。

entries.definition: to say in advance that something will happen. The verb names the act; the noun names the act or its content.
entries.definitionCN: 预言；预测。动词命名行为，名词命名行为或其内容。

entries.definition: able to be foreseen because it follows a pattern. It describes the thing, not the forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 可预测的。它描述被预测之物有规律，而非描述预报。

entries.definition: dependence on a substance or habit. It shares dicere 'say' through Latin addictio 'a handing over', but has nothing to do with foretelling.
entries.definitionCN: 上瘾；成瘾。它经由拉丁 addictio“交出”共享 dicere，但与预言无关。

entries.definition: a statement of what is expected, usually from present data. It is close to prediction but commoner in weather and finance.
entries.definitionCN: 预报；预测。常指天气或金融，接近 prediction 但更常用于这两个领域。

entries.definition: an estimate of a future value obtained by extending current trends. It stresses method, not certainty.
entries.definitionCN: 推算；预计。强调延长现有趋势的方法，而非确定性。

entries.definition: a prediction claimed to come from divine or special insight. It carries authority that a scientific prediction does not.
entries.definitionCN: 预言。声称来自神启或特殊洞察，带有科学预测所没有的权威。

entries.definition: an opinion offered without firm evidence. It lacks the evidential base that prediction usually implies.
entries.definitionCN: 猜测。指没有坚实证据的看法，缺少 prediction 通常暗含的证据基础。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pre- 'before' plus dict 'say' gives 'said before it happens', which is the whole meaning in two pieces.
normal.cn: pre-“在前”加 dict“说”，就是“在发生之前说出”，整个词义由两块拼成。

normal.en: The family predict, predictable, prediction and predictor all keep the same dict stem.
normal.cn: predict、predictable、prediction、predictor 全族保留同一 dict 词干。

normal.en: Scientific usage adds a test: a prediction must be able to fail.
normal.cn: 科学用法加了一条检验：预测必须有可能失败。

normal.en: Model prediction and weather forecast are the same forward arrow, one computed, one observed.
normal.cn: 模型预测与天气预报是同一支前箭头，一个算出来，一个看出来。

normal.en: The opposite word is retrodiction, a statement about the past made from present evidence.
normal.cn: 反面的词是 retrodiction（逆测），即用现在证据推断过去。

abstract.en: Picture an arrow drawn from today into an empty box marked tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 想象一支箭从今天射进标着“明天”的空格。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map where the isobars continue past the right edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，等压线一直画到纸的右边缘之外。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player saying the next three moves out loud.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手把接下来三步大声说出来。

examples.en: The report's prediction of a dry summer was correct.
examples.cn: 报告关于干旱夏季的预测是正确的。

examples.en: Every prediction from the model comes with an error range.
examples.cn: 模型的每一个预测都附带误差范围。

examples.en: A theory is valued for the predictions it makes possible.
examples.cn: 一个理论的价值在于它能带来哪些预测。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞迪克”音近 prediction：扑上去、锐利地、迪克先开口——抢在事情前头说 → prediction 预测

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ dicere“说、告诉”→ praedicere“预先说出”→ praedictio；英语取 predictio(n-) 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all point one arrow forward in time, but differ in who is speaking and what backs the claim.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把同一支箭指向未来，差别在谁在说、凭什么说。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a note about tomorrow written today.
core.cn: 核心意象：今天写好的一张关于明天的纸条。

branches.en: STATEMENT AND ACT: the noun names both what is said and the saying of it.
branches.cn: 陈述与行为：这个名词既指说出的内容，也指说的行为。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a testable forecast and the philosophical pairing with explanation are the same demand for evidence.
branches.cn: 科学：可检验的预报与哲学上同解释的配对，都是同一个证据要求。

branches.en: CALCULATED FUTURE: model output and trend extension both produce a future number from present data.
branches.cn: 算出的未来：模型输出与趋势延长都用现在数据算出未来数字。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: prophecy is prediction backed by claimed inspiration rather than evidence.
branches.cn: 权威：预言是靠声称的灵感而非证据支撑的预测。

branches.en: STAKES: betting turns a prediction into a commitment with a cost.
branches.cn: 代价：下注把预测变成带成本的承诺。

intro.en: Prediction is pre- plus the dic- stem plus -ion. The prefix marks time, the stem marks speech, and the suffix turns the act into a noun.
intro.cn: prediction 由 pre- 加 dic- 词干加 -ion 构成。前缀标记时间，词干标记言说，后缀把行为变成名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is dicere 'say' → praedicere 'foretell' → praedictio 'a foretelling'. The same dicere also yields diction, verdict and contradict.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线为 dicere“说”→ praedicere“预言”→ praedictio“预言”。同一 dicere 还产出 diction、verdict、contradict。

items.example: No one can predict the winner.

items.meaningCN: 预测；预言（-ion 动作名词）
items.example: The prediction failed within a week.
items.exampleCN: 这个预测一周内就落空了。
他的反应完全可以预料。

items.meaning: a person who predicts, or a variable used to predict
items.meaningCN: 预测者；预测变量（-or 施事或工具名词）
items.example: Age was the strongest predictor of relapse.
items.exampleCN: 年龄是复发最强的预测变量。

items.example: The two reports contradict each other.
The jury reached a verdict at noon.
items.exampleCN: 陪审团中午作出了裁决。

definition_zh: 预测性的；有预报作用的
definition_en: relating to or able to foretell something, especially in the phrase predictive of or predictive value
core_image: 一块试金石放在桌上，旁边摆着结果卡片：石头一碰，卡片就翻出未来的颜色
scene: The gene is predictive of heart disease but does not cause it.
sceneCN: 这里 predictive 是「能预示……的」（第 2 个义项：可用于预告某结果）；句意：这个基因能预示心脏病，但并不导致心脏病。图中可辨识物件：试金石、结果卡片、基因双螺旋图案。

pos.zh: 预测性的；有预报作用的

senses.title: Serving to foretell
senses.titleCN: 预测性的：用来预告的
senses.definition: having the function of saying what will happen before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 具有在事件发生前说明将会发生什么的功能
senses.example: The chapter is predictive rather than descriptive.
senses.exampleCN: 这一章是预测性的，而非描述性的。
senses.why: -ive marks a function. So predictive describes a tool, method or signal whose job is foretelling, not the foretelling itself.
senses.whyCN: -ive 标记功能。所以 predictive 描述承担预报任务的工具、方法或信号，而不是预报本身。

senses.title: Predictive of a result
senses.titleCN: 能预示某结果的
senses.definition: used with of to say that one thing is a sign that another thing will follow
senses.definitionCN: 与 of 连用，表示一事物是另一事物将会出现的信号
senses.example: Low attendance is predictive of failure in the final exam.
senses.exampleCN: 出勤率低预示着期末考试不及格。
senses.why: The of construction makes the word a bridge: a visible sign here, an outcome there. The grammar itself carries the inference.
senses.whyCN: of 结构把词变成桥：此处可见的迹象，指向彼处的结果。推论由语法本身承担。

senses.title: Statistical model quality
senses.titleCN: 模型质量：预测得准不准
senses.definition: describing a model's capacity to estimate correctly values that are not yet observed
senses.definitionCN: 描述模型正确估计尚未观测值的能力
senses.example: The predictive accuracy of the model fell when the market changed.
senses.exampleCN: 市场变化后，模型的预测准确度下降了。
senses.why: Machine learning measures a model by future performance, so the adjective becomes a score: predictive accuracy, predictive power.
senses.whyCN: 机器学习以未来表现衡量模型，因此这个形容词变成一种分数：预测准确度、预测力。

senses.title: Predictive validity
senses.titleCN: 预测效度：测出来的分数管不管用
senses.definition: in testing, the extent to which a score forecasts later performance
senses.definitionCN: 在测验中，分数能预告后续表现的程度
senses.example: The admissions test has good predictive validity for first-year grades.
senses.exampleCN: 这项入学考试对一年级成绩有良好的预测效度。
senses.why: Psychometrics needed a term for a test that predicts rather than describes. Predictive validity names that specific evidence relation.
senses.whyCN: 心理测量学需要一个词指“预测而非描述”的测验。预测效度命名了这一特定的证据关系。

senses.title: Predictive text and coding
senses.titleCN: 输入法联想：猜你要打什么
senses.definition: describing software that suggests the next word or symbol from patterns already typed
senses.definitionCN: 描述根据已输入的模式提示下一个词或符号的软件功能
senses.example: Predictive text guessed the word before she finished typing.
senses.exampleCN: 她还没打完，联想输入就猜出了这个词。
senses.why: The software repeats the same act as a human forecaster, only faster: from what has come, infer what comes next.
senses.whyCN: 软件重复了人类预报者的动作，只是更快：从已出现的推断下一个。

senses.title: Predictive maintenance
senses.titleCN: 预测性维护：坏之前先修
senses.definition: describing inspection scheduled from sensor data that indicate coming failure
senses.definitionCN: 描述依据传感器数据显示的即将故障而安排的检修
senses.example: Predictive maintenance cut unplanned downtime by half.
senses.exampleCN: 预测性维护把非计划停机减少了一半。
senses.why: Industry applies the word to machines: a vibration reading predicts a broken bearing, so repair moves before the breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 工业界把词用到机器上：振动读数预示轴承将坏，于是维修被挪到故障之前。

senses.title: Predictive policing
senses.titleCN: 预测性警务：按概率布警力
senses.definition: describing the use of data analysis to forecast where crime is likely, a practice that raises ethical questions
senses.definitionCN: 描述用数据分析预报犯罪可能发生地点的做法，该做法引发伦理争议
senses.example: Predictive policing shifted patrols to three districts.
senses.exampleCN: 预测性警务把巡逻转向了三个区。
senses.why: The adjective extends from objects to people and places, and that extension is exactly where the ethical debate begins.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从物件扩展到人和地点，而伦理争论正始于这一扩展。

senses.title: Predictive processing
senses.titleCN: 预测加工：大脑先猜再修正
senses.definition: in cognitive science, describing the view that perception works by constantly predicting input and correcting errors
senses.definitionCN: 在认知科学中描述“知觉靠不断预测输入并修正误差”的观点
senses.example: Predictive processing treats perception as correction of a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 预测加工理论把知觉视为对猜测的修正。
senses.why: The theory takes the word literally: the brain speaks before the world answers, then revises.
senses.whyCN: 该理论字面地使用这个词：大脑先于世界作答，然后再修正。

intro.en: Predictive is predict plus -ive, from Latin praedicere 'to say beforehand' (prae- 'before' + dicere 'say'). The suffix -ive comes from Latin -ivus and marks a capacity or function.
intro.cn: predictive 是 predict 加 -ive，源自拉丁 praedicere“预先说出”（prae-“在前”+ dicere“说”）。后缀 -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus，标记能力或功能。

items.en: dicere 'to say' is the base. It also gives diction, verdict and contradict, and is distinct from dicare 'to dedicate'.
items.cn: dicere“说”是基础词根，还产出 diction、verdict、contradict，与 dicare“奉献”不同。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus dicere gives praedicere, 'to say in advance'. The prefix fixes the forward time direction.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 dicere 得 praedicere“预先说出”。前缀固定了朝前的时间方向。

items.en: English forms the verb predict in the 16th century from the Latin participle stem praedict-.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪以拉丁分词词干 praedict- 构成动词 predict。

items.en: -ive, from Latin -ivus, marks what a thing can do. Predictive therefore means 'having the power to foretell', not 'the foretelling itself'.
items.cn: -ive 来自拉丁 -ivus，标记事物能做什么。因此 predictive 意为“具备预报能力”，而非“预报本身”。

items.en: Statistics, psychometrics and computing turn the adjective into a measure: predictive power, predictive validity, predictive accuracy.
items.cn: 统计学、心理测量学与计算把该形容词变成一种度量：预测力、预测效度、预测准确度。

items.en: Predictive text, predictive maintenance and predictive policing extend the word from forecasts of nature to forecasts of behaviour.
items.cn: 联想输入、预测性维护与预测性警务把该词从对自然的预报扩展到对行为的预报。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dict- stem or the -ive ending; the near-meaning group also looks forward but differs in whether a forecast is made.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dict- 词干或 -ive 结尾；近义组也朝前看，差别在是否作出预报。

entries.definition: the forecast itself. The noun is the thing said; the adjective is the capacity to say it.
entries.definitionCN: 预测本身。名词是被说出的东西，形容词是说出的能力。

entries.definition: the part of a sentence that says something about the subject. It comes from praedicare 'to proclaim', a different branch of the same dicere.
entries.definitionCN: 谓语。来自 praedicare“宣告”，是同一 dicere 的另一条分支。

entries.definition: relating to reasoning from general rules to particular cases. It ends in -ive but comes from ducere 'to lead', not dicere.
entries.definitionCN: 演绎的。虽以 -ive 结尾，但来自 ducere“引导”，不是 dicere。

entries.definition: accurately foretelling what will happen, often with a tone of inspiration. It stresses revelation rather than method.
entries.definitionCN: 预言式的；有预见的。强调启示色彩，而非方法。

entries.definition: done in expectation of something, before it happens. It describes preparation, not a forecast.
entries.definitionCN: 预先的；提前行动的。它描述准备，不是预报。

entries.definition: relating to the likely course of a disease. It is predictive in a specifically medical sense.
entries.definitionCN: 预后的；关于病程的。是医学意义上的预测。

entries.definition: used to identify a condition already present. It looks at now, while predictive looks at next.
entries.definitionCN: 诊断的。它判断当前已有的状况，而 predictive 看下一步。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ive means 'having the function of', so predictive means 'functioning as a forecast'.
normal.cn: -ive 意为“具有……功能”，所以 predictive 意为“起预报作用”。

normal.en: The fixed phrase predictive of shows the grammar doing the work: a sign now, a result later.
normal.cn: 固定搭配 predictive of 让语法承担工作：现在有迹象，以后有结果。

normal.en: Predictive validity is a test score that predicts grades, not one that describes them.
normal.cn: 预测效度指能预告成绩的分数，而不是描述成绩的分数。

normal.en: Predictive maintenance repairs before the breakdown, which is the industrial version of the same idea.
normal.cn: 预测性维护在故障前修理，是同一想法的工业版本。

normal.en: The contrast pair is diagnostic versus predictive: know now versus know next.
normal.cn: 对照词对是诊断与预测：知道现在与知道下一步。

abstract.en: Picture a smoke alarm: it does not report a fire, it reports the fire that is coming.
abstract.cn: 想象一个烟雾报警器：它不报告火灾，它报告正在到来的火灾。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow before a person: the shadow arrives first and tells you who is next.
abstract.cn: 想象人之前的影子：影子先到，告诉你谁要来。

abstract.en: Picture a weather glass whose falling column speaks before the storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一支气压表，水银柱下降先于风暴开口。

examples.en: The survey has predictive power for later earnings.
examples.cn: 这项调查对后来的收入有预测力。

examples.en: High cortisol is predictive of burnout in this sample.
examples.cn: 在这个样本中，皮质醇偏高预示着职业倦怠。

examples.en: We need a predictive model, not another description of the past.
examples.cn: 我们需要一个预测模型，而不是又一份对过去的描述。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑瑞滴克替吾”音近 predictive：先扑上去、锐利地滴出答案，替你预告——有预测作用 → predictive 预测性的

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ dicere“说”→ praedicere“预先说出”；praedict- 词干 + -ive（拉丁 -ivus，表功能）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe something that works as a signpost, pointing from present data to a later result.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“充当路标”的东西，从现在的数据指向后来的结果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a touchstone that reveals what is coming.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块能显出后事的试金石。

branches.en: SIGN AND FUNCTION: the general function and the 'predictive of' link are the adjective's two grammar shapes.
branches.cn: 标志与功能：一般功能与“预示”搭配是这个形容词的两种语法形态。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: model accuracy and test validity both turn foresight into a score.
branches.cn: 度量：模型准确度与测验效度都把预见变成分数。

branches.en: MACHINE AND MIND: predictive text guesses the next word, and predictive processing says the brain does the same.
branches.cn: 机器与心智：联想输入猜下一个词，预测加工说大脑也在做同样的事。

branches.en: INDUSTRY: maintenance moves before failure once a reading can foresee it.
branches.cn: 工业：一旦读数能预见故障，维护就提前到故障之前。

branches.en: SOCIAL RISK: policing by prediction extends the word to places and people, and to ethics.
branches.cn: 社会风险：以预测布警把词扩展到地点与人，也扩展到伦理。

intro.en: Predictive is predict + -ive. The prefix pre- marks time, the dic- stem marks saying, and -ive marks the capacity, giving a word for tools that foretell.
intro.cn: predictive 是 predict 加 -ive。前缀 pre- 标记时间，dic- 词干标记言说，-ive 标记能力，合起来指能预报的工具。

latinIntro.en: Latin dicere 'say' → praedicere 'foretell'. English keeps the stem dict- and adds -ive, from -ivus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 dicere“说”→ praedicere“预言”。英语保留 dict- 词干并加 -ive（来自 -ivus）。

items.exampleCN: 经济学家预测增长放缓。

items.example: The marker is predictive of relapse.

items.meaningCN: 以预测的方式（-ly 副词）
items.example: The term is used predictively, not descriptively.
items.exampleCN: 该词用于预测，而非描述。

items.meaning: one who predicts or a forecasting variable
items.example: Body mass is a strong predictor.
items.exampleCN: 体重是一个强的预测变量。

items.example: The system is unpredictable under stress.
items.exampleCN: 该系统在压力下不可预测。

items.meaningCN: 可预测性（-ity 抽象名词）
items.exampleCN: 可预测性有助于市场运转。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 预言性的（晚期拉丁构成）

definition_zh: 准备；预备；配制品；（复数）筹备工作
definition_en: the act of making something or someone ready, or a substance made ready for a particular use
core_image: 厨房案板上一排切好的食材、一张写满步骤的纸，锅还没上火
scene: Preparation for the exam took longer than the exam itself.
sceneCN: 这里 preparation 是「准备工作、预备」（第 1 个义项：使事情就绪的过程）；句意：备考所花的时间比考试本身还长。图中可辨识物件：切好的食材、步骤纸、尚未点火的锅。

pos.zh: 准备；预备；配制品；筹备工作

senses.title: Making ready
senses.titleCN: 准备：把事情弄成就绪状态
senses.definition: the process of getting something or someone ready for what is to come
senses.definitionCN: 使某物或某人就绪以应对将来之事的过程
senses.example: Preparation of the venue began three days early.
senses.exampleCN: 场地准备工作提前三天开始。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus parare 'make ready' gives praeparare, 'to make ready beforehand'. The noun names that before-work.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 parare“使就绪”构成 praeparare“预先使就绪”，名词命名这件“提前做的事”。

senses.title: The state of readiness
senses.titleCN: 预备状态：已经就绪
senses.definition: the condition of being ready, considered as a result rather than an activity
senses.definitionCN: 已经就绪的状态，被视为结果而非活动
senses.example: The troops were in preparation for a night march.
senses.exampleCN: 部队正处于夜行军的准备状态。
senses.why: The same -ation noun can name the result as well as the process, so preparation can be a state one is in.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ation 名词既可命名过程也可命名结果，所以 preparation 也可以是一种所处的状态。

senses.title: Study beforehand
senses.titleCN: 事先用功：备课、备考
senses.definition: work done in advance to learn or to be able to teach a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为学会或能够讲授某科目而提前做的工夫
senses.example: Her lesson preparation takes two hours a night.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚备课要花两个小时。
senses.why: Teaching turns preparation into a private, daily task: the teacher must be ready before the class exists.
senses.whyCN: 教学把准备变成私人的日常功课：课还不存在时，老师就得先就绪。

senses.title: A medicinal preparation
senses.titleCN: 药剂：配好的药
senses.definition: a substance, especially a medicine or cosmetic, compounded into a usable form
senses.definitionCN: 调配成可用形态的物质，尤指药物或化妆品
senses.example: The pharmacy makes a preparation for dry skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这家药房配制一种用于干性皮肤的制剂。
senses.why: Pharmacists prepare mixtures, so the product of that work took the name of the work. A preparation is readiness made tangible.
senses.whyCN: 药剂师调配混合物，于是产物沿用了动作的名字。制剂就是被做成实物的“就绪”。

senses.title: Laboratory preparation
senses.titleCN: 实验室制备：把样本弄成能看的样子
senses.definition: the treatment of a specimen or chemical so that it can be examined or used
senses.definitionCN: 对标本或化学品进行处理，使其可被观察或使用
senses.example: Slide preparation must be done within an hour of sampling.
senses.exampleCN: 玻片制备必须在采样后一小时内完成。
senses.why: In the lab the word names a technical routine: tissue, soil or a compound is made ready for the instrument.
senses.whyCN: 在实验室里，这个词命名一套技术流程：组织、土壤或化合物被做成适合仪器的样子。

senses.title: Food preparation
senses.titleCN: 食品加工：把原料做成饭
senses.definition: the cleaning, cutting and cooking of food before it is eaten
senses.definitionCN: 食物食用前的清洗、切配与烹制
senses.example: Food preparation areas must be kept separate from toilets.
senses.exampleCN: 食品加工区必须与卫生间分开。
senses.why: Cooking is preparation in the oldest sense: raw material is made ready to be consumed.
senses.whyCN: 烹饪是最古老意义上的准备：原料被做成可以入口的样子。

senses.title: Music: preparing a dissonance
senses.titleCN: 音乐：为不协和音做铺垫
senses.definition: in counterpoint, the earlier sounding of a note that will later form a dissonance
senses.definitionCN: 对位法中，某音先以协和状态出现，随后才构成不协和
senses.example: The suspension needs a preparation in the preceding chord.
senses.exampleCN: 延留音需要在前面和弦中有铺垫。
senses.why: Music theory borrowed the everyday word literally: the ear is prepared for the clash by hearing the note first in peace.
senses.whyCN: 乐理字面借用了日常词：先让耳朵在协和中听到该音，为后面的冲突做准备。

senses.title: Arrangements, plural
senses.titleCN: 筹备事项：一件件安排
senses.definition: the practical arrangements made in advance, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 提前做出的一项项实际安排，通常用复数
senses.example: The wedding preparations filled the whole summer.
senses.exampleCN: 婚礼筹备占满了整个夏天。
senses.why: Countable plural preparations names the individual items of the before-work: bookings, lists, orders.
senses.whyCN: 可数复数 preparations 命名提前工作中的一件件具体事项：预订、清单、订单。

intro.en: Preparation comes from Latin praeparare 'to make ready beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus parare 'make ready, furnish'. The noun is praeparatio.
intro.cn: preparation 来自拉丁 praeparare“预先使就绪”，由 prae-“在前”加 parare“使就绪、置办”构成，名词为 praeparatio。

items.en: parare meant 'to make ready, prepare, furnish'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it is generally connected with a PIE root *pere- 'to produce, procure', which should be labelled as generally believed rather than certain.
items.cn: parare 意为“使就绪、预备、置办”。其更深来源不确定，一般认为与原始印欧语词根 *pere-“产出、取得”有关，应标“一般认为是”而非确定。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus parare produced praeparare, 'to get ready in advance'. The prefix adds time, not place.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 parare 构成 praeparare“提前弄好”。前缀加的是时间，不是地点。

items.en: The action noun praeparatio named both the act of readying and the state of being ready.
items.cn: 动作名词 praeparatio 既指“使就绪的行为”，也指“已就绪的状态”。

items.en: English borrows preparation in the 1300s through French, first in religious writing about preparing the soul.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪经法语借入 preparation，最早见于关于心灵预备的宗教写作。

items.en: From the 16th century a preparation is also a compound made ready by an apothecary, which is why the word can name a medicine.
items.cn: 16 世纪起，preparation 也指药剂师配好的复方，因此这个词可以命名一种药。

items.en: In modern English the word covers exam study, food handling, lab routines and event arrangements, all sharing the same before-work.
items.cn: 现代英语中，这个词覆盖备考、食品处理、实验室流程与活动筹备，共享同一件“提前做的事”。

note.en: The look-alike group shares par- or the pre- prefix; the near-meaning group also involves getting ready but differs in what is being readied.
note.cn: 形近组共享 par- 或 pre- 前缀；近义组也涉及就绪，差别在“让什么就绪”。

entries.definition: to make ready. The verb is the act; the noun is the act or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 准备。动词是动作，名词是动作或其产物。

entries.definition: introducing or leading up to something main. It describes position in a sequence, not the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 预备的；作为前导的。它描述顺序中的位置，而非准备工作本身。

entries.definition: a public procession. It comes from French parade 'display', from parer 'to adorn, arrange', a different branch of parare's sense range.
entries.definitionCN: 游行；阅兵。来自法语 parade“展示”，源于 parer“装饰、布置”，是 parare 词义范围中的另一分支。

entries.definition: the state of being prepared. It names only the condition, while preparation can also name the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 就绪状态。它只命名状态，而 preparation 还能命名活动。

entries.definition: the way things are put in order, or the plans made. It stresses organisation rather than readiness.
entries.definitionCN: 安排；布置。强调组织，而非就绪。

entries.definition: long instruction to build skill. It is preparation for a role, but it names the skill-building, not the readying.
entries.definitionCN: 训练。它是为某角色做的准备，但命名的是技能培养，而非就绪。

entries.definition: the basic work that makes later work possible. It is a kind of preparation, but stresses foundation.
entries.definitionCN: 基础工作。它是准备的一种，但强调打地基。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: pre- 'before' plus parare 'make ready' gives the whole idea: ready made before it is needed.
normal.cn: pre-“在前”加 parare“使就绪”，整个意思就出来了：在需要之前先弄好。

normal.en: The family prepare, prepared, preparatory, preparation all keep the par- stem.
normal.cn: prepare、prepared、preparatory、preparation 全族保留 par- 词干。

normal.en: A medicinal preparation is the pharmacist's work turned into a bottle.
normal.cn: 药物制剂就是药剂师的工作变成一瓶东西。

normal.en: In preparation for is the most common frame and always points forward in time.
normal.cn: “为……做准备”是最常见的框架，永远指向未来的时间。

normal.en: The opposite state is unprepared, which is simply readiness missing.
normal.cn: 反面的状态是 unprepared，就是“就绪”缺席。

abstract.en: Picture a stage set the night before, lit but empty.
abstract.cn: 想象演出前一晚的舞台：灯亮着，台上没人。

abstract.en: Picture a bag packed by the door, waiting for the morning.
abstract.cn: 想象门口放着一个收好的包，等天亮。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player arranging pieces before the clock starts.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手在计时开始前摆好棋子。

examples.en: Careful preparation saved the expedition from the storm.
examples.cn: 周密的准备使探险队免于风暴之灾。

examples.en: The lab keeps a preparation of the enzyme at four degrees.
examples.cn: 实验室在四摄氏度下保存该酶的制剂。

examples.en: Most of the work was preparation, not performance.
examples.cn: 大部分工作是准备，而不是表演。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞帕瑞”音近 preparation：普普通通也要先摆好、排一排——提前把东西弄齐 → preparation 准备

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ parare“使就绪、置办”（parare 更深来源不确定，一般认为出自印欧 *pere-“产出”）；praeparatio(n-) 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe work done before the main event, sometimes the work and sometimes what the work produced.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“主事之前做的功”，有时指功夫本身，有时指功夫的产物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a workbench laid out before anything is cooked.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没开火就已摆好的案板。

branches.en: ACT AND STATE: preparation names the process and the readiness it produces.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：preparation 命名过程以及它带来的就绪。

branches.en: DAILY READYING: lesson preparation and food preparation are both private, repeated before-work.
branches.cn: 日常就绪：备课与备餐都是私人的、反复的提前功夫。

branches.en: MADE SUBSTANCE: a medicine and a microscope slide are the noun's product side.
branches.cn: 制成之物：药剂与玻片是这个词的产物面。

branches.en: MUSIC: counterpoint prepares the ear for a clash by sounding the note first in peace.
branches.cn: 音乐：对位法先让音在协和中出现，为耳朵预备冲突。

branches.en: PLANS: countable preparations are the individual arrangements of the before-work.
branches.cn: 计划：可数复数指提前工作中的一件件安排。

intro.en: Preparation is prae- plus parare plus -ion. The prefix marks 'before', the verb marks 'readying', and the suffix turns it into a noun of action or result.
intro.cn: preparation 由 prae- 加 parare 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记“在前”，动词标记“使就绪”，后缀使其成为动作或结果名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin line is parare 'make ready' → praeparare 'prepare' → praeparatio 'a preparing'. English also keeps the adjective stem in preparatory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁线为 parare“使就绪”→ praeparare“准备”→ praeparatio“预备”。英语还在 preparatory 中保留形容词词干。

items.example: She prepared the room for the guests.
items.exampleCN: 她为客人准备好了房间。

items.meaning: the act or result of readying

items.exampleCN: 他就读于一所预备学校。

items.example: We were prepared for the worst.
items.exampleCN: 我们做好了最坏的准备。

items.meaningCN: 有助于准备的（-ive 表性质，现罕用）

items.meaning: informal for preparation or preparatory school
items.example: He did his prep before dinner.
items.exampleCN: 他在晚饭前做完了预习。

items.meaning: the state of being ready, especially for emergencies
items.meaningCN: 戒备状态；应急准备（-ness 状态名词）
items.exampleCN: 该机构推动灾害应急准备。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使就绪；置办；取得（更深来源不确定）

definition_zh: 保存；保护；维护；留存状态
definition_en: the act of keeping something in its original condition and safe from damage, decay or loss
core_image: 一只玻璃罐封着一枚老照片和一片果肉，罐外贴着标着年份的标签
scene: The preservation of the manuscript required a climate-controlled room.
sceneCN: 这里 preservation 是「保护、保全」（第 1 个义项：使事物免受损坏）；句意：这份手稿的保存需要一个恒温恒湿的房间。图中可辨识物件：密封玻璃罐、老照片、标着年份的标签。

pos.zh: 保存；保护；维护；留存状态

collocations.phrase: in a good state of preservation

senses.title: Keeping from harm
senses.titleCN: 保存：让它别坏掉
senses.definition: the act of keeping something safe from damage, decay or destruction
senses.definitionCN: 使某物免受损坏、腐烂或毁坏的行为
senses.example: Preservation of the wreck began with a survey of the site.
senses.exampleCN: 沉船的保护工作从现场勘测开始。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus servare 'keep safe' gives praeservare, 'to keep safe beforehand'. The noun names that guarding.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 servare“看护”构成 praeservare“预先保全”，名词命名这份看护。

senses.title: Food preservation
senses.titleCN: 食品保存：让食物过季还在
senses.definition: the treatment of food so that it does not spoil, by drying, salting, canning or cooling
senses.definitionCN: 通过干燥、盐腌、罐装或冷藏使食物不腐败的处理
senses.example: Salt was the main means of preservation before refrigeration.
senses.exampleCN: 在冷藏出现之前，盐是主要的保存手段。
senses.why: Food spoils through organisms and moisture, so preservation is a war against decay carried out before decay starts.
senses.whyCN: 食物因微生物与水分而腐坏，所以保存是一场在腐坏开始之前发动的战争。

senses.title: Heritage conservation
senses.titleCN: 文物保护：留住旧物
senses.definition: the professional care of buildings, objects and documents so that they survive for the future
senses.definitionCN: 对建筑、器物与文献的专业养护，使其留存给未来
senses.example: The preservation of the old library took six years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老图书馆的保护工程耗时六年。
senses.why: Heritage work uses preservation because the goal is not repair but keeping the original fabric intact.
senses.whyCN: 遗产保护用 preservation，因为目标不是修缮，而是让原有材料完整留存。

senses.title: Nature protection
senses.titleCN: 自然保护：让物种和栖息地留着
senses.definition: the protection of wildlife, habitats or natural resources from destruction
senses.definitionCN: 使野生动物、栖息地或自然资源免遭破坏
senses.example: The trust works on the preservation of wetland birds.
senses.exampleCN: 该信托机构致力于湿地鸟类的保护。
senses.why: Here the thing preserved is a living system, so the word shifts from objects to processes that must keep running.
senses.whyCN: 这里被保存的是活的系统，词义从物件转向必须持续运转的过程。

senses.title: Legal and archival keeping
senses.titleCN: 证据与档案保全
senses.definition: the duty or practice of keeping records and evidence unaltered for later use
senses.definitionCN: 为日后使用而保持记录与证据未被改动的义务或做法
senses.example: The court ordered the preservation of all emails.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令保全所有电子邮件。
senses.why: Law cares about alteration, not decay. Preservation here means the object stays exactly as it was when the dispute began.
senses.whyCN: 法律关心的是改动，不是腐坏。这里的保存意味着物件保持在争议开始时的原样。

senses.title: Self-preservation
senses.titleCN: 自我保护：先保住自己
senses.definition: the instinct or action of keeping oneself alive or unharmed
senses.definitionCN: 使自己存活或不受伤害的本能或行动
senses.example: Self-preservation made him lie about the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 出于自我保护，他在事故上撒了谎。
senses.why: The compound self-preservation turns the word inward: the thing guarded and the guard are the same person.
senses.whyCN: self-preservation 把词转向内部：被保护之物与保护者都是同一个人。

senses.title: Condition of an object
senses.titleCN: 保存状况：东西还挺完整
senses.definition: the degree to which an old object has survived intact, as in a good state of preservation
senses.definitionCN: 旧物完整留存的程度，如“保存状况良好”
senses.example: The coins were found in a remarkable state of preservation.
senses.exampleCN: 这些硬币被发现时保存状况极好。
senses.why: English uses the noun for the result as well as the act, so preservation can be a property of the thing itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语用这个名词兼指结果与动作，所以 preservation 也可以是事物自身的属性。

senses.title: Digital preservation
senses.titleCN: 数字保存：别让文件读不出来
senses.definition: the work of keeping digital files readable as formats and hardware change
senses.definitionCN: 在格式与硬件更替中保持数字文件可读的工作
senses.example: Digital preservation means migrating files before the software dies.
senses.exampleCN: 数字保存意味着在软件淘汰之前迁移文件。
senses.why: Digital objects do not rot, they become unreadable, so preservation adds format migration to its older meaning.
senses.whyCN: 数字对象不会腐烂，而会变得读不出来，因此数字保存给旧词义加上了格式迁移。

intro.en: Preservation comes from Latin praeservare 'to keep safe beforehand', from prae- 'before' plus servare 'to watch over, keep'. The noun is praeservatio.
intro.cn: preservation 来自拉丁 praeservare“预先保全”，由 prae-“在前”加 servare“看守、保存”构成，名词为 praeservatio。

items.en: servare meant 'to watch over, keep safe, preserve'. It is generally traced to a PIE root *ser- 'to watch over', but the reconstruction is debated and should be labelled uncertain.
items.cn: servare 意为“看守、保全、保存”。一般追溯到原始印欧语 *ser-“看护”，但该重构有争议，应标注“来源不确定”。

items.en: servare 'keep safe' is not the same verb as servire 'to serve', which comes from servus 'slave'. Preserve and serve only look related in English.
items.cn: servare“保全”与 servire“服务”不是同一个动词，后者的来源是 servus“奴隶”。preserve 与 serve 只在英语中形近。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus servare gives praeservare, 'to guard in advance'. The prefix marks action taken before the danger arrives.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 servare 得 praeservare“提前看守”。前缀标记在危险到来之前采取的行动。

items.en: The action noun praeservatio named a keeping safe; medieval Latin used it in legal and medical senses.
items.cn: 动作名词 praeservatio 指保全；中世纪拉丁语把它用于法律与医学语境。

items.en: English borrows preservation through French, first for the keeping of food and of health.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 preservation，最初用于保存食物与维护健康。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries the word expands to buildings, wildlife and finally digital files, each with its own decay to fight.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，这个词扩展到建筑、野生动物，最终到数字文件，每一种都有自己的腐坏要对抗。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serv- shape, but only some share the root 'keep safe'; the near-meaning group all involve protecting something, with different aims.
note.cn: 形近组共享 serv- 外形，但只有部分共享“保全”词根；近义组都涉及保护，目的不同。

entries.definition: to keep safe from decay; also a reserved area or a fruit conserve. The verb is the act; preservation is the process or result.
entries.definitionCN: 保存；保护区；果酱。动词是动作，preservation 是过程或结果。

entries.definition: a substance added to prevent decay. It is the tool of preservation, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 防腐剂。它是保存的工具，不是过程。

entries.definition: work done for others. It comes from servire 'to serve' and servus 'slave', not from servare 'keep safe'.
entries.definitionCN: 服务。来自 servire“服务”与 servus“奴隶”，并非 servare“保全”。

entries.definition: the protection of nature or heritage, often with careful management and repair. It allows change; preservation prefers no change.
entries.definitionCN: 保护；养护。它允许修复与变动，而 preservation 更倾向于不加改动。

entries.definition: defence against harm. It stresses blocking a threat, while preservation stresses keeping a condition.
entries.definitionCN: 保护。强调挡住威胁，而 preservation 强调维持状态。

entries.definition: the act of keeping or holding on to something. It stresses not losing it, not keeping it intact.
entries.definitionCN: 保留；保有。强调不失去，而非保持完好。

entries.definition: the work of keeping something in good working order. It is continuous repair, where preservation is guarding from decay.
entries.definitionCN: 维护；保养。是持续的修理，而 preservation 是防腐败坏。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: servare means 'keep safe', so preservation is the noun of keeping, not of serving.
normal.cn: servare 意为“保全”，所以 preservation 是“保存”的名词，不是“服务”的名词。

normal.en: The family preserve, preservative, preserver and preservation all keep the serv- stem.
normal.cn: preserve、preservative、preserver、preservation 全族保留 serv- 词干。

normal.en: Food preservation, historic preservation and digital preservation are three battlefields against three kinds of decay.
normal.cn: 食品保存、历史保护、数字保存是三个战场，对抗三种腐坏。

normal.en: The phrase in a good state of preservation shows the noun naming a condition, not an act.
normal.cn: 短语“保存状况良好”显示该名词也能命名一种状态，而非动作。

normal.en: Self-preservation turns the word on the person doing the guarding.
normal.cn: 自我保护把词转向正在看护的那个人。

abstract.en: Picture a jar sealed with wax, the air kept outside and the fruit kept inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一只用蜡封住的罐子：空气挡在外面，果肉留在里面。

abstract.en: Picture a museum case where the light is dimmed so that colour will not fade.
abstract.cn: 想象博物馆的展柜把灯调暗，让颜色不褪。

abstract.en: Picture a copy of a file made before the old machine is switched off.
abstract.cn: 想象在老机器关机之前复制出的那份文件。

examples.en: Preservation of the wetland depends on keeping the water level stable.
examples.cn: 湿地的保护取决于保持水位稳定。

examples.en: The archive's preservation budget exceeds its acquisition budget.
examples.cn: 档案馆的保存预算超过了采购预算。

examples.en: Smoking meat is an old method of preservation.
examples.cn: 熏肉是一种古老的保存方法。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞则威神”音近 preservation：普普通通先“则”住、再“威”住它、像有神力护着——提前护住不让坏 → preservation 保存

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ servare“看守、保全”（servare 更深词源存疑）→ praeservare“预先保全”→ praeservatio；与 servire“服务”不同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all keep something from changing for the worse, whether the enemy is mould, time, law or a dead file format.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都让某物免于向坏的方向改变，无论敌人是霉菌、时间、法律还是失效的文件格式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sealed jar holding a year in place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只封住的罐子，把一个年份固定住。

branches.en: ACT AND CONDITION: the noun names the guarding and also the intact state that results.
branches.cn: 行为与状态：这个名词既命名看护，也命名由此得到的完好状态。

branches.en: BODY AND SELF: food kept from spoiling and a person kept alive both fight decay in the nearest frame.
branches.cn: 食物与自身：防止食物腐败与保住自己性命，都在最近的框里对抗腐坏。

branches.en: RECORDED PAST: a manuscript and a digital file both need active care or they vanish.
branches.cn: 被记录的过去：手稿与数字文件都需要主动养护，否则消失。

branches.en: LIVING SYSTEMS: wildlife preservation guards processes rather than objects.
branches.cn: 生命系统：野生动物保护守护的是过程，而非物件。

branches.en: LEGAL FIXITY: evidence preservation means keeping a record exactly as it was.
branches.cn: 法律上的固定：证据保全意味着让记录保持原样。

intro.en: Preservation is prae- plus servare plus -ion. The prefix marks action taken early, the verb marks keeping, and the suffix makes a noun of process or result.
intro.cn: preservation 由 prae- 加 servare 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记提前行动，动词标记看守，后缀构成过程或结果名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare 'keep safe' → praeservare 'guard beforehand'. The stem survives as preserv- in English, while servire 'serve' is a separate line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare“保全”→ praeservare“提前看守”。词干在英语中作 preserv-，而 servire“服务”是另一条线。

items.meaning: to keep from decay or loss
items.example: They preserved the timber with salt.

items.meaning: the act or state of being kept safe

items.meaningCN: 防腐剂（-ive 构成表物或性质的名词）
保存者；保护者（-er 施事名词）
items.example: He was a preserver of local songs.
items.exampleCN: 他是当地歌谣的保护者。

items.example: The preserved body was found in peat.
items.exampleCN: 这具保存下来的遗体发现于泥炭中。
自我保护的念头压过了他的诚实。
保护性养护允许适度修复。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 看守；保全（更深来源存疑）

definition_en: a substance added to food, wood or another material to prevent decay, or the adjective meaning 'serving to preserve'
core_image: 一小瓶透明液体倒进果酱罐里，罐外壁上的霉点立刻停住不动
scene: The label says the bread contains no preservative.
sceneCN: 这里 preservative 是「防腐剂」（第 1 个义项：防止腐败的添加物）；句意：标签上写着这款面包不含防腐剂。图中可辨识物件：小瓶液体、果酱罐、停在半路的霉点。

senses.title: A substance against decay
senses.titleCN: 防腐剂：加一点，坏得慢
senses.definition: a substance added to a product to stop it decaying or spoiling
senses.definitionCN: 加入产品中以防止其腐败变质的物质
senses.example: Nitrites are a common preservative in cured meat.
senses.exampleCN: 亚硝酸盐是腌肉中常用的防腐剂。
senses.why: The -ative suffix marks what does the work, so preservative is literally 'the thing that preserves'. The substance carries out the verb.
senses.whyCN: -ative 后缀标记“执行动作者”，所以 preservative 字面就是“起保存作用的东西”。物质在执行那个动词。

senses.title: Food additive
senses.titleCN: 食品添加剂中的那一类
senses.definition: a food additive whose function is shelf life rather than colour, texture or taste
senses.definitionCN: 食品添加剂中功能为延长保质期、而非调色调味的那一类
senses.example: Preservatives must be listed after the ingredients.
senses.exampleCN: 防腐剂必须列在配料之后。
senses.why: Regulation separates additives by function, and preservation is one function among several. The word becomes a legal category.
senses.whyCN: 法规按功能区分添加剂，保存是其中一项。这个词因此成为法律分类。

senses.title: Cosmetics and pharmacy
senses.titleCN: 化妆品与药品里的防腐
senses.definition: an ingredient that stops microbes growing in a cream, lotion or liquid medicine
senses.definitionCN: 阻止微生物在乳霜、洗液或药水中生长的成分
senses.example: Water-based creams need a preservative to stay safe.
senses.exampleCN: 水基乳霜需要防腐成分才能保持安全。
senses.why: Anything water-based can host bacteria. The preservative protects the user, not only the product.
senses.whyCN: 任何含水产品都可能滋生细菌。防腐剂保护的是使用者，不只是产品。

senses.title: Wood and materials
senses.titleCN: 木材防护：防虫防霉
senses.definition: a treatment applied to timber or fabric to resist insects, fungus and rot
senses.definitionCN: 涂于木材或织物以抗虫、抗真菌与抗腐朽的处理剂
senses.example: The fence was dipped in a copper preservative.
senses.exampleCN: 栅栏在铜盐防腐剂中浸过。
senses.why: The word leaves the kitchen and enters building work, where the same enemies appear: water, fungi and insects.
senses.whyCN: 这个词离开厨房进入建筑，敌人却相同：水、真菌与昆虫。

senses.title: Adjective: preserving
senses.titleCN: 形容词义：有保存作用的
senses.definition: used as an adjective for something that tends to preserve, now mostly in fixed phrases
senses.definitionCN: 作形容词表示“有保存倾向的”，现多用于固定短语
senses.example: The preservative effect of salt was known before chemistry.
senses.exampleCN: 盐的防腐作用在化学出现之前就已被知晓。
senses.why: The same -ative ending can describe a tendency rather than name a substance, so the word doubles as an adjective.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 -ative 结尾既可描述倾向，也可命名物质，所以这个词兼作形容词。

senses.title: Preservative-free claim
senses.titleCN: “不含防腐剂”的标签
senses.definition: used in marketing phrases that promise no added preservative, sometimes with a shorter shelf life
senses.definitionCN: 用于承诺未添加防腐剂的营销说法，往往意味着保质期更短
senses.example: The preservative-free version costs twice as much.
senses.exampleCN: 不含防腐剂的版本价格翻倍。
senses.why: A negative phrase can carry as much meaning as a positive one: no preservative means the product must be used quickly.
senses.whyCN: 否定短语与肯定短语同样有信息量：没有防腐剂意味着产品必须尽快用完。

senses.title: Vaccine preservative
senses.titleCN: 疫苗中的防腐成分
senses.definition: an antimicrobial added to multi-dose vaccine vials to prevent contamination between doses
senses.definitionCN: 加入多剂型疫苗瓶中以防剂量间污染的抗微生物成分
senses.example: Thimerosal was used as a preservative in some vaccines.
senses.exampleCN: 硫柳汞曾在一些疫苗中作防腐剂。
senses.why: Public health adds a new frame: the risk is contamination each time a vial is opened, so the substance guards the vial itself.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生加了新框架：风险在于每次开瓶的污染，所以该物质守护的是瓶子本身。

senses.title: Preservative versus additive
senses.titleCN: 与“添加剂”的区别
senses.definition: the class of additives defined by purpose, distinguished from colourings, emulsifiers and flavourings
senses.definitionCN: 按用途划分的一类添加剂，区别于着色剂、乳化剂与调味剂
senses.example: Not every additive is a preservative, though every preservative is an additive.
senses.exampleCN: 并非所有添加剂都是防腐剂，但所有防腐剂都是添加剂。
senses.why: Classification works by function. Preservation is one job in the additive toolbox, which is why the two words nest rather than overlap.
senses.whyCN: 分类按功能划分。保存是添加剂工具箱中的一项工作，所以两词是包含关系，而非重叠。

intro.en: Preservative is formed on Latin praeservare 'to keep safe beforehand' (prae- 'before' + servare 'keep safe') plus the suffix -ative, from Latin -ativus.
intro.cn: preservative 由拉丁 praeservare“预先保全”（prae-“在前”+ servare“保全”）加后缀 -ative（来自拉丁 -ativus）构成。

items.en: servare 'to watch over, keep safe' is the base of the family. Its further root is uncertain; the usual PIE *ser- reconstruction is debated and should be marked uncertain.
items.cn: servare“看守、保全”是词族的基础。其更深词根不确定，常见的原始印欧语 *ser- 重构有争议，应标“来源不确定”。

items.en: prae- 'before' plus servare gives 'to guard in advance'. The prefix explains why preservation begins before decay.
items.cn: prae-“在前”加 servare 得“提前看守”。前缀解释了为何保存要在腐坏之前开始。

items.en: -ativus in Latin marks a capacity or an agent, as in 'serving to do'. English -ative keeps that double role, so a preservative can be a thing or a quality.
items.cn: 拉丁 -ativus 标记能力或施事，意为“用于做……的”。英语 -ative 保留这双重角色，所以 preservative 既可指物，也可指性质。

items.en: English records preservative first as an adjective meaning 'having the power to preserve', then as a noun for a substance.
items.cn: 英语最早把 preservative 记为形容词“有保存能力的”，随后作为物质名词使用。

items.en: In the 19th and 20th centuries chemical preservatives expand with canning and long-distance food trade, and regulation follows.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪，化学防腐剂随罐装与远距离食品贸易扩张，相关法规随之出现。

items.en: Late 20th century labelling turns the word into a consumer signal, with preservative-free claims on the front of the pack.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，标签让这个词成为消费信号，包装正面出现“不含防腐剂”的说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the serv- stem or the -ative ending; the near-meaning group all protect something, but not all are substances.
note.cn: 形近组共享 serv- 词干或 -ative 结尾；近义组都起保护作用，但不都是物质。

entries.definition: the act or state of being kept safe. It names the process; preservative names the agent that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 保存的行为或状态。它命名过程，preservative 命名执行过程的物质。

entries.definition: to keep from decay. The verb is the action the substance performs.
entries.definitionCN: 保存；保护。它是该物质执行的动作。

entries.definition: favoring tradition and resisting change. It shares servare through conservare 'keep together', but means social caution, not decay prevention.
entries.definitionCN: 保守的。它经由 conservare“共同保存”共享 servare，但指社会态度上的谨慎，不是防腐败坏。

entries.definition: any substance added to a product for a purpose. A preservative is one kind of additive.
entries.definitionCN: 添加剂。指为某目的加入产品的任何物质，防腐剂是其中一种。

entries.definition: a substance that slows oxidation. It is a preservative working by one specific chemical route.
entries.definitionCN: 抗氧化剂。它通过特定化学途径起防腐作用。

entries.definition: a substance that kills microbes on the body. It protects health, while a preservative protects the product.
entries.definitionCN: 抗菌剂；消毒剂。它保护健康，而防腐剂保护产品。

entries.definition: a substance that keeps a product's structure or mixture from changing. It prevents separation rather than decay.
entries.definitionCN: 稳定剂。它防止结构或混合物分离，而非防止腐败。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: -ative marks the agent, so a preservative is the thing that does the preserving.
normal.cn: -ative 标记施事，所以 preservative 就是“做保存这件事的东西”。

normal.en: Food, cosmetics, wood and vaccines all use the word because all four can host microbes or rot.
normal.cn: 食品、化妆品、木材、疫苗都用这个词，因为四者都可能滋生微生物或腐烂。

normal.en: Preservative-free is a fixed label phrase and always implies a shorter shelf life.
normal.cn: 不含防腐剂是固定标签短语，总意味着保质期更短。

normal.en: The nesting is one-way: every preservative is an additive, but not every additive preserves.
normal.cn: 包含关系是单向的：所有防腐剂都是添加剂，但并非所有添加剂都起保存作用。

normal.en: The adjective use survives in preservative effect, where the word describes a quality rather than a bottle.
normal.cn: 形容词用法保留在“防腐作用”这类短语里，描述的是性质而不是一瓶东西。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose hands are held still by a drop of oil.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴油把钟表的指针按住不动。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed envelope that keeps air away from a photograph.
abstract.cn: 想象一只封好的信封，把空气挡在照片之外。

abstract.en: Picture salt crystals surrounding a fish, taking the water out before the microbes can use it.
abstract.cn: 想象盐粒包围一条鱼，在微生物利用水分之前把水抽走。

examples.en: The jam contains only fruit, sugar and one preservative.
examples.cn: 这种果酱只含水果、糖和一种防腐剂。

examples.en: Preservative-treated timber lasts far longer outdoors.
examples.cn: 经防腐处理的木材在户外耐用得多。

examples.en: Some preservatives are harmless in small doses and problematic in large ones.
examples.cn: 有些防腐剂小剂量无害，大剂量则有问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普瑞泽沃提夫”音近 preservative：普普通通的东西先“则”住、再“沃”住水、最后“提”住不坏——加进去防腐败 → preservative 防腐剂

root: 拉丁 prae-“在前”+ servare“保全”（更深词源存疑）→ praeservare“预先保全”；praeservat- 词干 + -ative（拉丁 -ativus，表施事或能力）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe an agent that slows decay, and the differences come from where the decay would happen.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“让腐坏变慢的施事”，差别在腐坏本来会发生在哪里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop that stops mould in its tracks.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴让霉菌停住的液体。

branches.en: AGENT AND QUALITY: the noun names the substance, the adjective names its tendency, and both come from one suffix.
branches.cn: 施事与性质：名词命名物质，形容词命名倾向，两者出自同一后缀。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: as an additive class, the word is defined by purpose rather than by chemistry.
branches.cn: 分类：作为添加剂的一类，它按用途而非化学成分定义。

branches.en: PROTECTING USERS: creams and multi-dose vials are guarded because they touch people.
branches.cn: 保护使用者：乳霜与多剂瓶被防护，因为它们接触人体。

branches.en: MATERIALS: wood and cloth meet the same enemies as food, so the same word serves.
branches.cn: 材料：木材与织物面对与食物相同的敌人，所以沿用同一个词。

branches.en: MARKETING: the negative label phrase turns absence into a selling point.
branches.cn: 营销：否定式标签把“没有”变成卖点。

intro.en: Preservative is the Latin stem preservat- plus -ative. The stem carries 'keep safe', and the suffix marks either the agent or the quality.
intro.cn: preservative 是拉丁词干 preservat- 加 -ative。词干携带“保全”，后缀标记施事或性质。

latinIntro.en: Latin servare 'keep safe' → praeservare 'guard beforehand' → praeservativus. English keeps the stem preservat- throughout the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 servare“保全”→ praeservare“提前看守”→ praeservativus。英语全族保留 preservat- 词干。

items.example: Preservation of the site is urgent.
items.exampleCN: 该遗址的保护十分紧迫。

items.meaning: a substance or quality that preserves

items.example: She is a preserver of old recipes.
Preserved lemons are common in North Africa.

items.exampleCN: 新鲜无花果几乎无法保存。

items.meaning: careful protection of nature or heritage
items.exampleCN: 保护团体反对这条公路。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 看守；保全（更深来源存疑）

definition_zh: 普遍存在；流行程度；（流行病学）患病率
definition_en: the fact of being widespread or common, or in epidemiology the proportion of a population that has a condition at a given time
core_image: 一张地图上同一种颜色的点越铺越密，最后几乎连成一片
scene: The prevalence of the infection rose sharply among schoolchildren.
sceneCN: 这里 prevalence 是「流行程度、患病率」（第 1 个义项：某种情况在人群中的普遍程度）；句意：这种感染在学龄儿童中的患病率急剧上升。图中可辨识物件：逐渐变密的地图色点、连成一片的色块。

pos.zh: 普遍存在；流行程度；患病率

senses.title: Being widespread
senses.titleCN: 普遍存在：到处都有
senses.definition: the quality of existing widely in a place or group
senses.definitionCN: 在某地或某群体中广泛存在的性质
senses.example: The prevalence of mobile phones changed how people queue.
senses.exampleCN: 手机的普及改变了人们排队的方式。
senses.why: prae- 'before' plus valere 'be strong' gives praevalere, 'to be stronger, prevail'. What prevails is everywhere, so prevalence names wide existence.
senses.whyCN: prae-“在前”加 valere“强壮”构成 praevalere“更强、占优势”。占优势者处处都在，因此 prevalence 命名“广泛存在”。

senses.title: Epidemiological prevalence
senses.titleCN: 流行病学上的患病率
senses.definition: the proportion of a population that has a disease or condition at a particular time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻人群中患某病或具备某状况的比例
senses.example: The prevalence of diabetes in the region is eleven percent.
senses.exampleCN: 该地区糖尿病的患病率是百分之十一。
senses.why: Epidemiology needed a word for how much disease is present now, as distinct from how fast new cases appear.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学需要一个词指“现在有多少病”，以区别于“新病例出现得多快”。
