definition_zh: 专业地；以专业方式；在职业层面
definition_en: in a way that shows the standards, training or conduct of a profession, or as a paid occupation
core_image: 一名穿工装的技术员把手套戴正、工具排成一行，才开始动那台精密仪器
scene: The building was professionally restored, not patched up by amateurs.
sceneCN: 这里 professionally 是「以专业方式」（第 1 个义项：按行业标准来做）；句意：这座建筑是专业修复的，不是业余人士草补的。图中可辨识物件：工装、排成一行的工具、精密仪器。

pos.zh: 专业地；以专业方式；在职业层面

senses.title: By professional standards
senses.titleCN: 以专业方式：按行规来做
senses.definition: in a manner that meets the accepted standards and ethics of a profession
senses.definitionCN: 以符合某行业公认标准与职业伦理的方式
senses.example: The team handled the complaint professionally and in writing.
senses.exampleCN: 团队以专业方式并以书面形式处理了投诉。
senses.why: A profession is literally a public declaration, so professionally means doing the work in a way one could declare openly.
senses.whyCN: profession 字面是“公开声明”，所以 professionally 指以“可以公开承认的方式”做事。

senses.title: As a paid occupation
senses.titleCN: 在职业层面：靠这个吃饭
senses.definition: as one's main paid work rather than as a hobby or an occasional activity
senses.definitionCN: 作为主要的有酬工作，而非爱好或偶发活动
senses.example: She plays the cello professionally.
senses.exampleCN: 她以拉大提琴为职业。
senses.why: The adverb separates livelihood from amateur interest, which is why sport and music use it for the paid level.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把生计与业余兴趣分开，所以体育与音乐用它指有偿的职业层级。

senses.title: With trained skill
senses.titleCN: 以受训的技能：手上有功夫
senses.definition: using the specific technique acquired through formal training
senses.definitionCN: 运用通过正规训练获得的专门技术
senses.example: The wound was professionally dressed within minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 伤口在几分钟内就被专业地包扎好了。
senses.why: Training turns an ordinary act into a specialised one. The adverb credits the technique, not the intention.
senses.whyCN: 训练把普通动作变成专门动作。这个副词归功于技术，而不是意图。

senses.title: Professionally qualified
senses.titleCN: 具备专业资质：有证有资格
senses.definition: with the formal certification or licence a profession requires
senses.definitionCN: 具备该行业要求的正式认证或执照
senses.example: Only professionally qualified staff may sign the report.
senses.exampleCN: 只有具备专业资质的人员才能签署报告。
senses.why: Licensing makes professionalism visible and checkable, so the adverb attaches to credentials as well as behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 执照让专业素养可见、可核查，因此这个副词既附着于行为，也附着于资格。

senses.title: Professionally managed
senses.titleCN: 由专业人士管理
senses.definition: describing an organisation run by trained managers rather than by owners alone
senses.definitionCN: 描述由受过训练的管理者而非仅由业主运营的组织
senses.example: The fund is professionally managed and independently audited.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金由专业人士管理并接受独立审计。
senses.why: Ownership and management split in modern firms, and the adverb marks the arrival of trained management.
senses.whyCN: 现代企业把所有权与管理权分开，这个副词标记“受训管理者”的介入。

senses.title: Professionally speaking
senses.titleCN: 从专业角度说
senses.definition: used to mark a judgment made from within a field's standards rather than from personal opinion
senses.definitionCN: 用于标记依据某领域标准而非个人看法作出的判断
senses.example: Professionally speaking, the design is sound but the budget is not.
senses.exampleCN: 从专业角度看，这个设计是可靠的，但预算不行。
senses.why: The phrase claims authority without claiming certainty: the speaker steps into the role of the profession.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语借权威而不借确定性：说话人步入“行业角色”的位置。

senses.title: Professional conduct
senses.titleCN: 表现得专业：态度也算
senses.definition: in a way that maintains composure, confidentiality and respect for rules
senses.definitionCN: 以保持冷静、保密与遵守规则的方式
senses.example: He disagreed with the client but remained professionally courteous.
senses.exampleCN: 他不同意客户的意见，但仍保持专业的礼貌。
senses.why: Conduct is part of the standard. One can be professionally wrong, which is why the adverb often appears in complaints.
senses.whyCN: 行为本身就是标准的一部分。人可以“专业地犯错”，所以这个副词常出现在投诉语境。

senses.title: Professional-level sport
senses.titleCN: 职业水准：付费的赛场
senses.definition: in sport, describing competition at the paid elite level rather than the amateur level
senses.definitionCN: 在体育中指有偿的精英层级，而非业余层级
senses.example: He raced professionally for six seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 他以职业车手身份比赛了六个赛季。
senses.why: Sport uses the word for the money line, which is the clearest everyday boundary between professional and amateur.
senses.whyCN: 体育用这个词标记“收费线”，这是职业与业余最清楚的日常界线。

intro.en: Professionally is professional plus -ly. Professional comes from profession, from Latin professio 'a public declaration', from profiteri 'to declare openly' (pro- 'forth' + fateri 'to admit, declare').
intro.cn: professionally 是 professional 加 -ly。professional 来自 profession，源自拉丁 professio“公开声明”，而 professio 出自 profiteri“公开宣称”（pro-“向前”+ fateri“承认、宣告”）。

items.en: fateri meant 'to admit, confess, declare'. It is related to fari 'to speak', the source of fable and fame.
items.cn: fateri 意为“承认、供认、宣告”。它与 fari“说话”相关，后者是 fable 与 fame 的来源。

items.en: pro- 'forth' plus fateri gives profiteri, 'to declare publicly'. A profession was originally a public vow or declaration of a way of life.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 fateri 构成 profiteri“公开宣告”。profession 最初指公开立誓或宣告某种生活方式。

items.en: professio named the declaration itself and later the calling one declared. Medieval Latin applied it to the learned callings.
items.cn: professio 指宣告本身，后指所宣告的志业。中世纪拉丁语用它指有学问的职业。

items.en: English takes profession in the 14th century for a religious vow, then for the learned occupations of law, medicine and divinity.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入 profession 指宗教誓愿，后指法律、医学、神学等有学问的职业。

items.en: professional appears in the 19th century as the paid callings multiply; professionally follows as the -ly adverb.
items.cn: 19 世纪随着有偿职业增多，professional 出现；副词 professionally 随后由 -ly 构成。

items.en: In the 20th century the adverb shifts from 'by occupation' to 'to accepted standards', which is its dominant sense today.
items.cn: 20 世纪，这个副词从“以职业身份”转向“按公认标准”，这是今天的主要义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the fess- stem or the -ly ending; the near-meaning group all describe good conduct, differing in the standard invoked.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fess- 词干或 -ly 结尾；近义组都描述良好表现，差别在所依据的标准。

entries.definition: relating to a profession, or a person in one. The adjective describes the person or standard; the adverb describes how something is done.
entries.definitionCN: 专业的；专业人士。形容词描述人或标准，副词描述做事方式。

entries.definition: a paid calling requiring training, or a public declaration. It names the field the adverb refers to.
entries.definitionCN: 职业；行业；公开声明。它命名副词所指向的领域。

entries.definition: a statement admitting guilt. It shares fateri 'declare' but uses con- 'together', and means admitting, not practising a calling.
entries.definitionCN: 供认；忏悔。共享 fateri“宣告”，但用 con-“共同”，指承认，不是执业。

entries.definition: with great skill. It stresses competence, while professionally stresses standards and conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 熟练地。强调能力，而 professionally 强调标准与行为。

entries.definition: well enough to do the job. It is a lower bar than professionally and carries no ethical claim.
entries.definitionCN: 胜任地。标准低于 professionally，且不含伦理要求。

entries.definition: according to official rules or ceremony. It stresses procedure, not occupational standards.
entries.definitionCN: 正式地。强调程序，而非行业标准。

entries.definition: in the manner of an unpaid or untrained enthusiast. It is the direct contrast of the paid, trained sense.
entries.definitionCN: 业余地。它是“有偿且受训”这一义的直接对照。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: profession is a public declaration, so professionally means doing work you could declare in public.
normal.cn: profession 是公开声明，所以 professionally 指做“可以公开承认”的工作。

normal.en: The pair professional and amateur is the clearest boundary: one is paid and trained, the other is not.
normal.cn: 专业与业余是最清楚的界线：一个有偿且受训，一个不是。

normal.en: Professionally qualified and professionally managed both attach the adverb to credentials and systems, not just manners.
normal.cn: 具备专业资质与由专业人士管理，都把副词附着于资格与制度，而不只是礼数。

normal.en: Professionally speaking borrows the authority of a field for one sentence.
normal.cn: 从专业角度说是为了一句话借用某个领域的权威。

normal.en: The opposite unprofessional describes conduct that breaks the standard rather than lacking skill.
normal.cn: 反义词 unprofessional 描述违反标准的行为，而非缺少技能。

abstract.en: Picture a toolbox where every tool has its own marked place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个工具箱，每件工具都有标记好的位置。

abstract.en: Picture a signature at the bottom of a report, written by someone licensed to write it.
abstract.cn: 想象报告底部那个签名，出自有资格签署的人。

abstract.en: Picture a referee who keeps the same face whether the call favors or hurts.
abstract.cn: 想象一名裁判，无论判罚有利还是不利都保持同一张脸。

examples.en: The site is professionally monitored during the excavation.
examples.cn: 发掘期间现场由专业人员监测。

examples.en: She answered the hostile question professionally.
examples.cn: 她以专业的方式回答了那个敌意提问。

examples.en: Professionally speaking, the sample is too small to support the claim.
examples.cn: 从专业角度说，这个样本太小，支持不了该主张。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若费神纳利”音近 professionally：专业的人做事要先“费神”、再按“纳利”的规矩来——按行规办事 → professionally 专业地

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ fateri“宣告”（与 fari“说话”相关）→ profiteri“公开宣称”→ professio“职业、声明”；professional + -ly。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all invoke a standard outside the individual, whether it is training, licence, conduct or the paid line.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都援引个人之外的标准，无论是训练、执照、行为规范还是有偿界线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tools laid out before the work begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：动工之前排好的工具。

branches.en: STANDARD AND CONDUCT: doing the task right and behaving right are two halves of the same professional claim.
branches.cn: 标准与行为：把活做对与把人做对，是同一专业主张的两半。

branches.en: PAID LINE: music and sport both use the adverb to separate paid elite from amateur.
branches.cn: 有偿界线：音乐与体育都用这个副词区分有偿精英与业余。

branches.en: TRAINING AND LICENCE: skill is learned, and credentials make it checkable.
branches.cn: 训练与执照：技能靠学习，资格让它可核查。

branches.en: SYSTEMS: professionally managed marks trained management inside an organisation.
branches.cn: 制度：由专业人士管理标记组织内受训的管理层。

branches.en: AUTHORITY: professionally speaking steps into the role of the field for one judgment.
branches.cn: 权威：从专业角度说，是为一个判断步入行业角色。

intro.en: Professionally is profession plus -al plus -ly. The Latin stem profess- carries 'declared', and the two suffixes turn it into an adjective and then an adverb.
intro.cn: professionally 是 profession 加 -al 加 -ly。拉丁词干 profess- 携带“已宣告”，两个后缀先构成形容词，再构成副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fateri 'declare' → profiteri 'declare publicly' → professio 'declaration, calling'. English builds profession, professional, professionally.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 fateri“宣告”→ profiteri“公开宣称”→ professio“声明、志业”。英语构成 profession、professional、professionally。

items.example: He professed ignorance of the deal.
items.exampleCN: 他声称对这桩交易不知情。
这个案子处理得很专业。

items.meaning: the conduct and standards of a profession
items.exampleCN: 员工表现出真正的专业精神。
该联赛于 1992 年职业化。

definition_en: the process of moving forward step by step, or an ordered sequence of stages, numbers or chords
core_image: 一排台阶向远处升高，每一级上都刻着下一个数字
scene: The progression from trainee to manager took eight years.
sceneCN: 这里 progression 是「进程、逐步发展」（第 1 个义项：一级一级向前推进）；句意：从实习生到经理的进程用了八年。图中可辨识物件：逐级升高的台阶、台阶上的数字、远处的台阶尽端。

senses.title: Forward movement in steps
senses.titleCN: 进程：一级一级往前
senses.definition: the act of moving forward through a series of stages
senses.definitionCN: 通过一系列阶段向前推进的行为
senses.example: The progression from symptom to diagnosis was slow.
senses.exampleCN: 从出现症状到确诊的进程很慢。
senses.why: pro- 'forward' plus gradi 'to walk' gives progredi, 'to go forward'. The noun names a walking forward that happens in steps.
senses.whyCN: pro-“向前”加 gradi“行走”构成 progredi“前行”。名词命名一步一步向前走的动作。

senses.title: An ordered sequence
senses.titleCN: 序列：先后次序本身
senses.definition: the order in which things follow one another, considered apart from the movement
senses.definitionCN: 事物相互接续的次序，被视为独立于移动过程
senses.example: The chapters form a clear progression of ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 这些章节构成清晰的思想序列。
senses.why: Once steps are numbered, the word can name the ladder instead of the climbing.
senses.whyCN: 一旦给台阶编号，这个词就可命名梯子本身，而不是攀爬。

senses.title: Gradual development
senses.titleCN: 逐步发展：慢慢变成另一个样子
senses.definition: a series of small changes that add up to a larger transformation
senses.definitionCN: 一系列小变化累积成较大转变
senses.example: The city's progression from port to financial centre took a century.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市从港口发展为金融中心用了一个世纪。
senses.why: Gradual change is progress measured in small gradi, each step small enough to be unremarkable alone.
senses.whyCN: 渐变是以细小步伐衡量的前进，每一步单独看都不起眼。

senses.title: Mathematics: a progression
senses.titleCN: 数学：数列、级数
senses.definition: a sequence of numbers in which each term follows the previous by a fixed rule, as in arithmetic or geometric progression
senses.definitionCN: 按固定规则由前一项得到后一项的数列，如等差或等比数列
senses.example: The terms form an arithmetic progression with a difference of three.
senses.exampleCN: 这些项构成公差为三的等差数列。
senses.why: Mathematics abstracts the staircase into numbers: each step adds or multiplies by the same amount.
senses.whyCN: 数学把台阶抽象成数字：每一步加或乘同一个量。

senses.title: Music: chord progression
senses.titleCN: 音乐：和弦进行
senses.definition: the sequence of chords through which a piece moves
senses.definitionCN: 一首乐曲依次经过的和弦序列
senses.example: The song uses a simple four-chord progression.
senses.exampleCN: 这首歌用了简单的四和弦进行。
senses.why: Harmony moves in steps too, so musicians borrowed the walking word for the order of chords.
senses.whyCN: 和声也按步移动，所以音乐家借用了“行走”的词来指和弦次序。

senses.title: Clinical progression
senses.titleCN: 病程进展：病往哪儿走
senses.definition: in medicine, the way a disease develops or worsens over time
senses.definitionCN: 医学上指疾病随时间发展或加重的过程
senses.example: The scan shows progression of the lesion.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示病灶有进展。
senses.why: Clinical use is directional but not positive: progression here can mean getting worse, which shows the word names movement, not improvement.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法有方向但不含正面意义：这里进展可以指恶化，说明这个词命名移动，而非改善。

senses.title: Career progression
senses.titleCN: 职业晋升：一级一级上去
senses.definition: the movement from one job level or role to a higher one
senses.definitionCN: 从一个职位层级或角色向更高层级移动
senses.example: The company publishes a clear career progression path.
senses.exampleCN: 公司公布了一条清晰的职业晋升路径。
senses.why: Workplaces turn the staircase into job grades, so progression becomes a synonym for promotion over time.
senses.whyCN: 职场把台阶变成职级，因此 progression 成为随时间晋升的同义词。

senses.title: Logical progression
senses.titleCN: 论证递进：一步接一步
senses.definition: the order in which an argument or narrative moves from one point to the next
senses.definitionCN: 论证或叙述从一个要点推进到下一个要点的次序
senses.example: The essay lacks a logical progression between paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章段落之间缺少逻辑递进。
senses.why: Reasoning also walks: each claim should stand on the one before, which is why writers speak of a progression of ideas.
senses.whyCN: 推理也在行走：每个主张应站在前一个之上，所以写作者说“思想递进”。

intro.en: Progression comes from Latin progressio 'a going forward', from progredi 'to go forward', built on pro- 'forward' plus gradi 'to walk, step'.
intro.cn: progression 来自拉丁 progressio“向前行走”，源于 progredi“前行”，由 pro-“向前”加 gradi“行走、迈步”构成。

items.en: gradi meant 'to walk, step, go'. Its noun gradus 'step' gives grade, gradual and degree, so the family is built on the single step.
items.cn: gradi 意为“行走、迈步、前进”。其名词 gradus“步”产出 grade、gradual、degree，整个词族都建立在“一步”上。

items.en: pro- 'forward' plus gradi gives progredi, 'to go forward'. The prefix fixes direction; the verb supplies the walking.
items.cn: pro-“向前”加 gradi 构成 progredi“前行”。前缀固定方向，动词提供“走”。

items.en: The action noun progressio named a going forward, and could also mean a literary or logical advance.
items.cn: 动作名词 progressio 指向前行进，也可指文辞或论证上的推进。

items.en: English borrows progression through French, first for physical advance and then for the order of events.
items.cn: 英语经法语借入 progression，先指物理前进，后指事件次序。

items.en: In the 17th century mathematics fixes arithmetic and geometric progression as names for number sequences.
items.cn: 17 世纪数学固定了等差数列与等比数列作为数列的名称。

items.en: Later centuries add clinical progression and chord progression, extending the staircase to disease and harmony.
items.cn: 此后几个世纪加入病程进展与和弦进行，把台阶扩展到疾病与和声。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the grad- stem or the pro- prefix; the near-meaning group all involve moving forward, differing in pace and direction.
note.cn: 形近组共享 grad- 词干或 pro- 前缀；近义组都涉及向前，差别在速度与方向。

entries.tag: same root, verb or mass noun
entries.definition: forward movement or improvement, usually uncountable. Progression stresses the step-by-step series.
entries.definitionCN: 前进；进步，通常不可数。progression 强调一步一步的序列。

entries.definition: happening gradually, or favoring reform. The adjective describes the manner or the politics.
entries.definitionCN: 渐进的；进步的。形容词描述方式或政治立场。

entries.definition: hostile or forceful. It comes from ad- 'toward' plus gradi, 'to step toward', and has nothing to do with progress.
entries.definitionCN: 攻击性的。来自 ad-“朝向”加 gradi“迈步”，与 progress 无关。

entries.definition: a set of things in a fixed order. It names the arrangement, while progression can name the moving through it.
entries.definitionCN: 序列。它命名排列，而 progression 可命名在其中推进的过程。

entries.definition: the process of growing or becoming more advanced. It stresses change in quality, not ordered steps.
entries.definitionCN: 发展。强调性质变化，不强调有序步骤。

entries.definition: a single movement forward or an improvement. It is one step, while progression is the series of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 前进；进展。它是一步，而 progression 是一系列步。

entries.definition: movement backward or return to an earlier state. It is the direct opposite of progression.
entries.definitionCN: 倒退；回归。它是 progression 的直接反面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: gradi 'walk' is the core, so a progression is a walk with numbered steps.
normal.cn: gradi“行走”是核心，所以 progression 是一次给每一步编号的行走。

normal.en: grade, gradual and degree all come from gradus 'step', which makes the staircase image easy to keep.
normal.cn: grade、gradual、degree 都出自 gradus“步”，台阶意象很好记。

normal.en: Arithmetic progression and geometric progression show the rule: add a constant or multiply by one.
normal.cn: 等差数列与等比数列显示规则：加一个常数，或乘一个常数。

normal.en: Chord progression is harmony walking from one chord to the next.
normal.cn: 和弦进行就是和声从一个和弦走到下一个。

normal.en: Clinical progression can mean getting worse, which proves the word is about movement, not improvement.
normal.cn: 病程进展可以指恶化，证明这个词关乎移动，而非改善。

abstract.en: Picture a staircase where each step is numbered one higher.
abstract.cn: 想象一级级台阶，每级数字比前一级大一。

abstract.en: Picture a film shown frame by frame rather than all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影逐帧播放，而不是一次全放。

abstract.en: Picture a path of stepping stones that only makes sense from the first stone onward.
abstract.cn: 想象一条踏石小径，只有从第一块石起才看得懂。

examples.en: The progression of the illness was faster than expected.
examples.cn: 病情进展比预期更快。

examples.en: Each term in the progression is double the one before.
examples.cn: 这个数列中每一项都是前一项的两倍。

examples.en: Her career progression followed a steady path through three departments.
examples.cn: 她的职业晋升沿着一条稳定路径，跨过三个部门。

dict_mnemonic.text: “普若格瑞神”音近 progression：一步一步“格”上去、像有“神”力推着走——逐级向前 → progression 进程

root: 拉丁 pro-“向前”+ gradi“行走”（名词 gradus“步”）→ progredi“前行”→ progressio；英语取 progression 词干 + -ion。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe movement or order in steps, whether the steps are stages, numbers, chords or arguments.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述“按步移动或按步排列”，无论步是阶段、数字、和弦还是论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: numbered steps climbing into the distance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一级级带编号的台阶伸向远方。

branches.en: WALK AND LADDER: the moving and the order are the verb side and the structure side of one image.
branches.cn: 行走与梯子：移动与次序是同一意象的动词面与结构面。

branches.en: GRADUAL CHANGE: many small steps add up to a new state.
branches.cn: 渐变：许多小步累积成新状态。

branches.en: RULES OF ORDER: numbers and chords both advance by a fixed rule.
branches.cn: 次序规则：数字与和弦都按固定规则推进。

branches.en: CLINICAL DIRECTION: progression can be worsening, which shows the word is neutral about value.
branches.cn: 临床方向：进展可以指恶化，说明这个词对价值是中性的。

branches.en: SOCIAL AND LOGICAL LADDERS: job grades and argument steps are both ordered climbing.
branches.cn: 社会与逻辑阶梯：职级与论证步骤都是有序攀爬。

intro.en: Progression is pro- plus gradi plus -ion. The prefix marks direction, the verb marks walking, and the suffix makes the series a noun.
intro.cn: progression 由 pro- 加 gradi 加 -ion 构成。前缀标记方向，动词标记行走，后缀把序列变成名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gradi 'walk' → progredi 'go forward' → progressio. The same gradi gives grade, gradual, ingredient and aggressive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gradi“行走”→ progredi“前行”→ progressio。同一 gradi 还产出 grade、gradual、ingredient、aggressive。

items.example: The progression of grades is automatic.
